Theoretical predictions showed close agreement with experimental measurements. Exact efficiency values and specific wavelength ranges are not provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second- and third-harmonic generation at structurally tailorable wavelengths without complex geometries or hybrid structures. The agreement between theory and experiment advances understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights metallic nanostructures as potential ultrafast UV and deep-UV light sources.

title: On stimulated scattering including harmonic generation in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths
summary: A fully nonlinear analysis for the growth rate of the stimulated backscatter instability of an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave with arbitrary polarization in an unmagnetized pair plasma is presented. The connection of this instability to the FEL process is discussed and utilized. An intense EM wave causes an initially stationary pair plasma to drift forward with a speed near the speed of light. The resulting distribution function for both cold and warm pair plasmas is presented. It is shown that the frequency of the reflected light is thus Doppler downshifted from that of the incident wave. For a linearly polarized EM wave there is also an additional contribution to the forward drift at its second harmonic which leads to backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler downshifted frequency for sufficiently cold pair plasmas. Fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show how the instability depends on the pair plasma temperature. The effect of the intensity profile of the incoming EM wave as well as implications for astrophysical pair plasmas is discussed.

AI.tldr: A fully nonlinear theory and PIC simulations show how intense electromagnetic waves drive stimulated backscatter and odd-harmonic generation in unmagnetized pair plasmas, with growth rates and spectra controlled by pump strength, polarization, and plasma temperature.
AI.motivation: To determine the growth rate of stimulated backscatter of an intense, arbitrarily polarized electromagnetic wave in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths, using its relation to the free-electron-laser process and assessing implications for astrophysical pair plasmas.
AI.method: Fully nonlinear analysis of the backscatter instability, derivation of distribution functions for cold and warm pair plasmas drifting near the speed of light, and fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations; the incoming wave intensity profile is also examined.
AI.result: The initially stationary pair plasma drifts forward near the speed of light, and reflected light is Doppler downshifted. For linear polarization, a second-harmonic forward-drift contribution produces backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler-downshifted frequency in sufficiently cold pair plasmas. PIC simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show temperature dependence.
AI.conclusion: The instability provides a nonlinear route to Doppler-downshifted backscatter and harmonic generation in pair plasmas; temperature and pump-profile effects are important, with implications for astrophysical pair plasmas and a discussed connection to free-electron-laser processes.

title: Peak Performance in Matched Filtering: Fused Correlation and Statistically Controlled Screening on CPUs and GPUs
summary: Batched matched filtering and cross-correlation over large template banks are a primary computational cost in gravitational-wave astronomy, seismology, and radio transient searches. Standard pipelines pair a general-purpose inverse Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with separate multiplication and peak-finding kernels, writing intermediate spectra and full correlation series to memory for every template. We fuse the conjugate product into the first inverse-transform butterflies and the peak reduction into the last so only candidate peaks leave processor registers, and tile batches in 2D so $K^2$ correlations reuse $2K$ cached spectra. This shifts filtering from a DRAM-bandwidth-bound to an on-chip cache-bandwidth-bound regime. In some situations, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is concentrated toward lower frequencies while higher frequencies dominate the transform length. We develop a hierarchical screening method that exploits this via a sequence of short low-frequency transforms before evaluating the full band, deriving stage thresholds from the spectral power profile and matched-filter noise autocovariance to target a specified false-dismissal probability. We demonstrate these methods in the open-source matchedfilter library across eight CPU architectures and two integrated GPUs (AMD Radeon 8060S via Vulkan and Apple M2 via Metal). On an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 at $N=4096$, fused peak-only filtering is $1.4\times$ faster than a standalone AOCL-FFTW inverse transform on one CPU core and $6.2\times$ faster than rocFFT on its Radeon 8060S GPU ($3.1\times$ over MLX FFT on the M2 GPU). For a fiducial gravitational-wave search ($ρ_\mathrm{th}=5.5$, $10^{-2}$ false-dismissal target), hierarchical screening yields a $26\times$ speedup over AOCL-FFTW on CPU, $21\times$ over rocFFT on the 8060S GPU, and $19\times$ over MLX FFT on the M2 GPU.

AI.tldr: The paper fuses matched-filter multiplication and peak reduction into inverse FFT stages, uses cache-aware batch tiling and statistically controlled hierarchical low-frequency screening, and reports substantial CPU and integrated-GPU speedups for gravitational-wave template-bank searches.
AI.motivation: Batched matched filtering and cross-correlation over large template banks are a primary computational cost in gravitational-wave astronomy, seismology, and radio transient searches. Standard pipelines use a general-purpose inverse FFT plus separate multiplication and peak-finding kernels, writing intermediate spectra and full correlation series to memory for every template.
AI.method: The authors fuse the conjugate product into the first inverse-transform butterflies and peak reduction into the last, so only candidate peaks leave processor registers, and tile batches in 2D so K^2 correlations reuse 2K cached spectra. They also develop hierarchical screening using short low-frequency transforms before the full band, with stage thresholds derived from the spectral power profile and matched-filter noise autocovariance to target a specified false-dismissal probability. The methods are demonstrated in the open-source matchedfilter library on eight CPU architectures and two integrated GPUs, AMD Radeon 8060S via Vulkan and Apple M2 via Metal.
AI.result: On an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 at N=4096, fused peak-only filtering is 1.4x faster than a standalone AOCL-FFTW inverse transform on one CPU core, 6.2x faster than rocFFT on the Radeon 8060S GPU, and 3.1x faster than MLX FFT on the M2 GPU. For a fiducial gravitational-wave search with rho_th=5.5 and a 10^-2 false-dismissal target, hierarchical screening yields 26x speedup over AOCL-FFTW on CPU, 21x over rocFFT on the 8060S GPU, and 19x over MLX FFT on the M2 GPU.
AI.conclusion: Fusing correlation and peak detection with inverse FFT butterflies shifts filtering from DRAM-bandwidth-bound to on-chip cache-bandwidth-bound operation, and hierarchical screening can provide large additional speedups while targeting a specified false-dismissal probability. The abstract does not provide detailed end-to-end detection-accuracy results beyond this screening control.

title: Experimental and numerical simulations of near resonant 2D soliton interaction in shallow water
comment: accepted for publication for Water Waves
summary: Experiments were carried out in {a} large wave basin ($27\times 30$\,m$^2$) to study the interactions of non-linear waves in shallow water (0.35\,m deep). A stereoscopic technique was used to measure the waves accurately over a vast area ($180$\,m$^2$). The numerical code {Tolosa-lct}, designed for simulating wave propagation in shallow water, reproduces the observations and extends the analysis for larger domains. The diffraction of oblique solitons is discussed. Mach interaction of two solitons occurs for some given incidence and amplitudes, producing a third soliton. A focus is made on the near resonant interaction of a soliton with a vertical wall. An example of a regular Mach interaction is shown, where a steady solution is achieved experimentally, with a maximum amplitude amplification of 3.2 at the wall.

AI.tldr: Large-basin experiments and Tolosa-lct simulations were used to study shallow-water nonlinear wave interactions, including oblique-soliton diffraction and near-resonant soliton interaction with a vertical wall; a steady Mach interaction produced a third soliton and amplitude amplification of 3.2 at the wall.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to improve understanding of nonlinear wave interactions in shallow water, particularly diffraction of oblique solitons and near-resonant Mach interaction of a soliton with a vertical wall.
AI.method: Experiments were performed in a 27 x 30 m2 wave basin with 0.35 m water depth. A stereoscopic technique measured waves over 180 m2. The Tolosa-lct numerical code, designed for shallow-water wave propagation, reproduced the observations and extended the analysis to larger domains.
AI.result: Mach interaction of two solitons occurred for certain incidence and amplitudes, producing a third soliton. For near-resonant interaction of a soliton with a vertical wall, a regular Mach interaction reached a steady experimental solution with maximum amplitude amplification of 3.2 at the wall.
AI.conclusion: The Tolosa-lct code reproduces the experimental observations and enables extended numerical analysis. The experiments demonstrate a steady near-resonant Mach interaction with significant amplitude amplification at a vertical wall.

title: Monolayer MoSe2 as an Attenuator of Spintronic Terahertz Emission
summary: Understanding ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion at ferromagnetic/2D interfaces is critical for developing THz-frequency spintronic devices such as ultrafast memories, sensors, and compact THz sources. We investigate this by studying spintronic THz emission (STE) from Py/Au heterostructures capped with transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer MoSe2 using time-domain THz spectroscopy. We observe a pronounced reduction in emitted THz amplitude when a monolayer MoSe2 flake covers Py/Au or Py/Pt emitters compared with uncovered regions. A consistent, approximately fourfold attenuation occurs for both systems, despite an order-of-magnitude larger THz radiation from the bare Py/Pt emitter. These results indicate that the suppression is independent of emitter strength. We attribute the attenuation to THz absorption by free charge carriers and trions that are either present due to charge transfer from the metallic layer or photoexcited by the laser pulse, which can significantly diminish the detectable STE signal. This finding provides an explanation for the discrepancy between weak STE signals from FM/TMD heterostructures and magnetotransport reports of sizable spin-orbit torques in similar systems, and highlights the need to account for photoinduced THz attenuation when interpreting ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion measurements in 2D TMD heterostructures.

AI.tldr: Monolayer MoSe2 deposited on Py/Au or Py/Pt strongly attenuates spintronic terahertz emission, approximately fourfold, largely independent of the bare emitter strength; the effect is attributed to THz absorption by free carriers and trions.
AI.motivation: Understanding ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion at ferromagnetic/2D interfaces is important for THz-frequency spintronic devices such as ultrafast memories, sensors, and compact THz sources.
AI.method: The authors studied spintronic THz emission from Py/Au heterostructures capped with monolayer MoSe2, and compared Py/Au and Py/Pt emitters, using time-domain THz spectroscopy; specific laser parameters are not provided in the abstract.
AI.result: A pronounced reduction in emitted THz amplitude occurs where monolayer MoSe2 covers Py/Au or Py/Pt compared with uncovered regions. An approximately fourfold attenuation is observed for both systems despite an order-of-magnitude larger THz radiation from bare Py/Pt, indicating that suppression is independent of emitter strength. The attenuation is attributed to THz absorption by free charge carriers and trions present due to charge transfer from the metal or photoexcitation by the laser pulse.
AI.conclusion: The findings help explain the discrepancy between weak spintronic THz emission from ferromagnetic/TMD heterostructures and magnetotransport reports of sizable spin-orbit torques in similar systems, and show that photoinduced THz attenuation must be considered when interpreting ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion measurements in 2D TMD heterostructures.

title: Self-consistent thermal-runaway electron equilibria
summary: In this work, we develop and solve a self-consistent equilibrium model for plasmas containing thermal and runaway electron (RE) populations, motivated by observations of residual plasma density during alternating-current (AC) transitions in ISTTOK. We adopt an existing monoenergetic, narrow-pitch guiding-center formulation, while retaining a spatially varying toroidal-field function, and show that prescribing the radius-weighted RE density by the orbit label alone conflicts with particle conservation and vector equilibrium wherever the thermal toroidal-field function varies along an occupied drift contour. Both conditions instead require the ratio of RE density to toroidal field to be constant along each drift contour. Taking this ratio as a function of the orbit label gives a compatible closure that relates the equilibrium RE density to a prescribed reference profile. Combined with Grad-Shafranov-Helmholtz thermal free functions, it yields a closed field equation that retains the displacement between drift and magnetic surfaces. At fixed thermal coefficients, we prove existence for every finite reference-profile amplitude under sign and spectral conditions. We also prove local constrained existence and uniqueness near a thermal equilibrium with a nonsingular current-beta response and derive a current-pressure bound. An ISTTOK ramp-down example with a prescribed 20% energetic-current fraction and 2 keV energy gives a magnetic-orbit axis separation of 2.39 mm. The resulting fields and current distributions can serve as initial conditions for studies of electron survival and plasma recovery through AC reversal.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a self-consistent equilibrium model for plasmas with thermal and runaway electron populations, derives a compatible closure requiring the runaway density-to-toroidal-field ratio to be constant along drift contours, proves existence and local uniqueness properties, and applies the model to an ISTTOK ramp-down case.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by observations of residual plasma density during alternating-current transitions in ISTTOK and the need for a self-consistent equilibrium description that includes both thermal and runaway electron populations.
AI.method: The authors adopt a monoenergetic, narrow-pitch guiding-center formulation while retaining a spatially varying toroidal-field function. They show that particle conservation and vector equilibrium require the ratio of runaway electron density to toroidal field to be constant along each drift contour, use this ratio as an orbit-label function for closure, and combine it with Grad-Shafranov-Helmholtz thermal free functions to obtain a closed field equation retaining drift-magnetic surface displacement. Local constrained existence and uniqueness are proved near a thermal equilibrium, and a current-pressure bound is derived. An ISTTOK ramp-down example with a prescribed 20% energetic-current fraction and 2 keV energy yields a magnetic-orbit axis separation of 2.39 mm.
AI.conclusion: The resulting fields and current distributions provide initial conditions for studies of electron survival and plasma recovery through alternating-current reversal.

title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
summary: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces PU-DDFEM, a partition-of-unity data-driven finite element method for anisotropic diffusion in magnetized plasmas, using local snapshot spaces, spectral mode extraction, and reusable conforming basis functions to reduce online cost for large-scale simulations.
AI.motivation: Extreme anisotropy in magnetized plasma transport makes diffusion along magnetic field lines much larger than perpendicular diffusion, producing thin steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods cannot resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement.
AI.method: The authors propose the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a bottom-up data-driven local model reduction approach with complete offline-online splitting. Local magnetic fields and boundary conditions are parametrized to build a snapshot space; dominant modes are extracted through a local spectral problem and mapped to the global domain via partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space.
AI.result: The abstract reports the construction of PU-DDFEM and states that its basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations. No quantitative numerical results or benchmark comparisons are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: PU-DDFEM is presented as a reusable reduced-order finite element framework for anisotropic diffusion in magnetized plasmas, intended to address severe anisotropy and boundary-layer resolution while lowering online computational cost; the abstract does not report experimental validation or performance metrics.

title: Variational Newton-Krylov descent for periodic orbits of two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow
comment: 42 pages, 18 figures, 5 tables. Supplementary material (catalogue of the solutions) as an ancillary file. Submitted to the Journal of Fluid Mechanics
summary: A matrix-free Newton-Krylov method for computing long unstable periodic orbits of turbulent flows is presented. The method arises from the space-time variational formulation of Lan & Cvitanović (Phys. Rev. E, vol. 69, 2004, 016217), and runs on graphics processing units with a preconditioner from time-spectral methods that retains advection. In two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow at $Re = 40$, near recurrences remain about as frequent at long periods as at moderate ones, and searches from them converge to 183 distinct solutions with periods up to 191, about forty escape times, all but one verified by multiple shooting. The primary question is then whether such a long orbit can be taken, on its own, as a proxy for the attractor, and thus capture the statistics of the turbulent flow. The mean dissipation and energy of the long orbits lie close to the medians of the flow, and the distribution of the dissipation along a long orbit is comparable with that of a turbulent segment of the same duration, except in its tail, which most orbits miss. Their leading Floquet exponents appear to lie slightly below the Lyapunov spectrum of the flow, as may be expected of quieter orbits. The typical distance of the turbulent flow from a long orbit decreases as the period grows, but with an unfavourable scaling set by the correlation dimension of the attractor, which suggests that ever longer orbits may be needed as the Reynolds number grows.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a GPU-based matrix-free Newton-Krylov method for long unstable periodic orbits of turbulent flows and applies it to two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow at Re = 40, finding 183 distinct orbits with periods up to 191. Long orbits reproduce median energy and dissipation statistics reasonably well but miss rare high-dissipation events, and their typical distance to the turbulent flow decreases with period at a rate limited by the attractor's correlation dimension.
AI.motivation: The study aims to compute long unstable periodic orbits in turbulent flows and determine whether a single sufficiently long orbit can serve as a proxy for the attractor and reproduce turbulent statistics.
AI.method: A matrix-free Newton-Krylov method is derived from the space-time variational formulation of Lan and Cvitanović, run on graphics processing units, and preconditioned with a time-spectral method that retains advection. It is applied to two-dimensional Kolmogorov flow at Re = 40, with searches initiated from near recurrences and solutions checked by multiple shooting.
AI.result: Near recurrences remain about as frequent at long periods as at moderate ones, and searches converge to 183 distinct solutions with periods up to 191, about forty escape times; all but one are verified by multiple shooting. Mean dissipation and energy of the long orbits are close to the flow medians, and dissipation distributions along long orbits resemble those of turbulent segments of equal duration except in the tail, which most orbits miss. Leading Floquet exponents appear slightly below the flow's Lyapunov spectrum. The typical distance of the turbulent flow from a long orbit decreases with period, but with unfavourable scaling governed by the attractor's correlation dimension.
AI.conclusion: Long periodic orbits can capture some bulk statistical properties of the turbulent flow, but they do not fully represent rare tail events. The unfavourable scaling of the distance between the flow and long orbits suggests that increasingly longer orbits may be required as the Reynolds number increases.

title: Thulium- and Holmium-Doped Silica Fibres for 2 μm High-Power and Highly-Efficient Lasers
summary: Silica optical fibres, originally developed as a low-loss transmission medium for telecommunications, have evolved into a versatile platform for compact and efficient high-power lasers. This review discusses recent progress in thulium- and holmium-doped active fibres emitting within the 2 μm spectral band, with an emphasis on material and waveguide approaches that address power scaling through thermal-load mitigation and enhanced laser efficiency. In particular, the temperature dependence of absorption and emission cross-sections are reviewed, and their implications for spectral gain, amplified spontaneous emission and high-power laser operation are discussed. Structured-core thulium fibres are then considered as a route to combining the high local Tm3+ concentration required for efficient two for- one cross-relaxation with a reduced average dopant concentration, lower longitudinal heat load, and a pedestal-free waveguide design. Finally, recent results on holmium-doped silica fibres prepared by nanoparticle-assisted modified chemical vapour deposition are summarised. Crucially, the Al/Ho ratio is identified as a key compositional parameter governing laser efficiency, while a high absolute alumina content supports a long fluorescence lifetime and enables high Ho3+ concentrations without excessive clustering. These advances have enabled core-pumped holmium fibre lasers with slope efficiencies reaching 84% and output powers approaching 100W. Collectively, these development illustrate how control of spectroscopy, composition, and transverse dopant distribution can extend the performance of silica fibre lasers across the 1.7-2.2 μm spectral region.

AI.tldr: This review covers thulium- and holmium-doped silica fibres for 2 μm high-power, high-efficiency lasers, focusing on thermal-load mitigation, temperature-dependent spectroscopy, structured-core Tm fibres, and nanoparticle-assisted MCVD Ho fibres; core-pumped Ho fibre lasers reached 84% slope efficiency and output powers approaching 100 W.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to address power scaling and efficiency in 2 μm silica fibre lasers by mitigating thermal load and improving spectroscopic and waveguide design.
AI.method: It reviews temperature-dependent absorption and emission cross-sections and their effects on spectral gain, amplified spontaneous emission, and high-power operation; considers structured-core Tm fibres to combine high local Tm3+ concentration for two-for-one cross-relaxation with reduced average doping and lower longitudinal heat load; and summarises Ho-doped silica fibres made by nanoparticle-assisted modified chemical vapour deposition, identifying the Al/Ho ratio and absolute alumina content as key compositional parameters.
AI.result: Core-pumped holmium fibre lasers achieved slope efficiencies reaching 84% and output powers approaching 100 W; high absolute alumina content supports a long fluorescence lifetime and enables high Ho3+ concentrations without excessive clustering.
AI.conclusion: Control of spectroscopy, composition, and transverse dopant distribution can extend the performance of silica fibre lasers across the 1.7-2.2 μm spectral region.

title: Impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation on L-H transition in the KSTAR tokamak
summary: The impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation (ERMP) on the low-to-high (L-H) confinement mode transition is investigated through dedicated experiments on the KSTAR tokamak with tungsten divertor and numerical simulations with a one-dimensional (1D) reduced transport model. Experimentally, under matched conditions, the ERMP inhibits the L-H transition, whereas the reference discharge without ERMP enters H-mode. The ERMP enhances edge electron temperature fluctuations and the turbulence decorrelation rate, and flattens the toroidal rotation, reducing the edge $E\times B$ velocity shear below the threshold required for turbulence suppression. An extended 1D predator-prey model, which incorporates toroidal flow evolution and realistic radial profile of the magnetic perturbation due to plasma response field, reproduces the experimental trends of enhanced turbulence, reduced ExB flow shear, and inhibited L-H transition. These findings contribute to a better understanding of how ERMP affects L-H transition dynamics in tungsten divertor environments and offer a valuable reference for the application of ERMP in current and future fusion devices.

AI.motivation: The paper aims to clarify how edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation affects L-H transition dynamics in tungsten divertor environments and to provide a reference for applying such perturbations in current and future fusion devices.
AI.method: Dedicated matched-condition experiments were performed on the KSTAR tokamak with a tungsten divertor, together with numerical simulations using an extended one-dimensional predator-prey transport model that incorporates toroidal flow evolution and a realistic radial profile of the magnetic perturbation due to the plasma response field.

ERMP enhanced edge electron temperature fluctuations and the turbulence decorrelation rate, flattened toroidal rotation, and reduced edge E×B velocity shear below the threshold required for turbulence suppression. The extended 1D model reproduced the enhanced turbulence, reduced E×B flow shear, and inhibited L-H transition.
AI.conclusion: ERMP can inhibit the L-H transition by weakening edge E×B flow shear and enhancing turbulence, improving understanding of ERMP effects in tungsten divertor environments and providing a reference for ERMP application in current and future fusion devices.

title: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics
summary: Driving lattice vibrations provides a direct route to manipulating electronic correlations through nonlinear electron-phonon coupling. Finding suitable driving fields, however, requires control over the coupled dynamics beyond a simple choice of pulse amplitude and frequency. Here we develop a differentiable framework that combines field optimization with neural-network prediction in a two-site electron-phonon model. We compare piecewise-constant, B-spline, feed-forward, and recurrent control parameterizations, optimized to increase the accumulated electronic double occupation. For the dissipation-free model at zero Hubbard interaction, all the methods increase double occupation, with the B-spline raising the mean total double occupation of approximately 30%. Alongside control optimization, a separate recurrent network learns to predict the next-step double occupation and phonon observables from their preceding values and the applied field. These results establish a computational proof of concept for shaping local electronic correlations through a phonon drive and identify a promising route toward learned models for nonequilibrium materials control.

AI.tldr: The authors build a differentiable optimization-plus-neural-network framework in a two-site electron-phonon model to design driving fields that enhance electronic double occupation, and separately train a recurrent network to predict next-step double occupation and phonon observables.
AI.motivation: Lattice vibrations offer a direct route to manipulating electronic correlations via nonlinear electron-phonon coupling, but finding suitable driving fields requires control over the coupled dynamics that goes beyond simply choosing pulse amplitude and frequency.
AI.method: A differentiable framework combining field optimization with neural-network prediction is developed in a two-site electron-phonon model. Four control parameterizations are compared - piecewise-constant, B-spline, feed-forward, and recurrent - all optimized to increase accumulated electronic double occupation. Separately, a recurrent network learns to predict the next-step double occupation and phonon observables from their preceding values and the applied field.

The recurrent network successfully learns next-step prediction of double occupation and phonon observables; the abstract does not report quantitative prediction errors.

title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
summary: Data-driven surrogate modeling has emerged as a powerful paradigm for accelerating computational fluid dynamics, and hierarchical U-shaped networks, which resemble the structure of classical Geometric Multigrid (GMG) methods, have become prevalent designs. Modern surrogates built on these designs achieve competitive accuracy at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers; however, accurate prediction of complex flows remains challenging, and no existing architecture leads across them. In such networks, the multigrid analogy mainly concerns the multi-resolution topology, while their components largely follow common vision practice. To address this, this study introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow fields on regular grids that spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network. Parameter-free down- and upsampling stand in for restriction and prolongation, and additive skip connections for coarse-grid correction, with normalization-free transfer and skip pathways. Within this macro-architecture, convolutions are used at the fine and intermediate resolutions and shifted-window attention at the coarsest, whose window partitioning is generalized to handle periodicity independently per axis. Evaluated on unseen test configurations across four unsteady and steady flow benchmarks against five representative baselines, SUMNO is best in 5 of 7 settings and ranks second in the remaining two. It reduces the 10-step rollout MSE by about 30% relative to the strongest baseline, and outperforms three baselines with over 130 million parameters using 9.4 million parameters.

AI.tldr: SUMNO is a multigrid neural operator that spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network for fluid-flow surrogate modeling, combining parameter-free restriction/prolongation, additive coarse-grid correction, convolutions, and coarsest-level shifted-window attention; it outperforms representative baselines on most tested flow settings with far fewer parameters.
AI.motivation: Data-driven surrogates can accelerate computational fluid dynamics, and U-shaped networks resemble geometric multigrid, but accurate complex-flow prediction remains difficult and no existing architecture leads across cases. The multigrid analogy in existing networks mainly concerns multi-resolution topology while their components largely follow common vision practice, motivating a more faithful multigrid neural operator design.
AI.method: The paper introduces SUMNO for fluid flow fields on regular grids. It spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network, using parameter-free downsampling and upsampling as restriction and prolongation, additive skip connections for coarse-grid correction, and normalization-free transfer and skip pathways. Convolutions are used at fine and intermediate resolutions, while shifted-window attention is used at the coarsest resolution, with window partitioning generalized to handle periodicity independently per axis.

title: Enhancing optomechanical oscillation amplitude and frequency comb bandwidth by intensity-modulated driving
comment: 17 pages, 6 figures. Main text: 11 pages, 5 figures. Appendices: 3 pages, 1 figure. Data and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23735060
summary: Self-sustained oscillations in optomechanical systems are attractive as compact, low-noise sources of GHz signals and optical frequency combs for integrated photonic circuits. For these applications, the achievable oscillation amplitude directly sets clock power and comb bandwidth. This work studies the maximum amplitude that can be reached through combinations of cavity backaction and modulated optical driving, with realistic resources. For an optically driven mechanical resonator, the oscillation amplitude saturates at a level set by the finite cavity bandwidth. We show that modulating the input intensity near the mechanical resonance frequency raises the achievable amplitude toward this limit at equal mean input power and cavity linewidth. We use a cycle-averaged energy-balance analysis to identify the added power that shifts the stable periodic orbit to larger amplitudes. Numerical integration of the full equations of motion confirms the enhancement across two decades of cooperativity and sideband-resolution ratios from 0.1 to 10. The relative increase in amplitude is largest near the self-oscillation threshold and in the sideband-unresolved regime, enabling threshold-free large-amplitude oscillation where backaction alone fails to do so. The enhanced amplitude leads to a larger modulation depth of the optical field, enabling broader frequency combs, with improved stability of the comb spacing. Intensity-modulated driving thus offers power-constrained platforms a simple open-loop route to larger mechanical amplitudes and enhanced comb bandwidth.

AI.tldr: Intensity-modulated optical driving is shown, via energy-balance analysis and full numerical simulations, to increase the amplitude of self-sustained optomechanical oscillations toward the cavity-bandwidth-imposed limit at equal mean input power and linewidth, thereby broadening optical frequency combs and improving comb-spacing stability.

title: Laser-Driven Electron Stripping from Nanoparticles in Plasma
summary: Laser wakefield accelerators use plasma wake waves to produce high-energy electron beams over short distances. Nanoparticles can trigger localized electron injection, with their size and density influencing the accelerated beam charge. However, the electron charge of a nanoparticle does not determine how much charge is stripped by the laser. Here we show that a quasistatic electrostatic model predicts laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles, in agreement with particle-in-cell simulations in vacuum and helium plasma. The model identifies a saturation density that increases with laser amplitude and decreases with nanoparticle radius, separating complete from partial stripping. Above this density, the stripped electron fraction decreases and the stripped charge approaches a finite limit. Multicycle pulses produce more stripped charge than the model predicts due to time-dependent electron dynamics. In helium plasma, plasma wake waves induce additional electron stripping. These results give an understanding of the scaling of laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles and could inform nanoparticle parameter selection for future nanoparticle-assisted laser wakefield accelerators.

AI.tldr: A quasistatic electrostatic model explains laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles, identifying a laser-amplitude- and nanoparticle-radius-dependent saturation density that separates complete from partial stripping; the model agrees with particle-in-cell simulations in vacuum and helium plasma, while multicycle pulses and plasma wake waves add stripping beyond the model.
AI.motivation: Nanoparticles can trigger localized electron injection in laser wakefield accelerators, and their size and density affect accelerated beam charge, but the electron charge of a nanoparticle does not determine how much charge the laser strips; a scaling understanding is needed to inform nanoparticle parameter selection for future nanoparticle-assisted laser wakefield accelerators.

The model identifies a saturation density separating complete from partial stripping; specific laser, nanoparticle, and simulation parameters are not provided in the abstract.

Above this density, the stripped electron fraction decreases while the stripped charge approaches a finite limit. Multicycle pulses produce more stripped charge than the model predicts because of time-dependent electron dynamics, and in helium plasma, plasma wake waves induce additional electron stripping.
AI.conclusion: The results provide an understanding of the scaling of laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles and could inform nanoparticle parameter selection for future nanoparticle-assisted laser wakefield accelerators.

title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Presented at ADT-ISMDDC-2026 (ICST-ODESA-2026), Odesa, Ukraine, September 22-24, 2026. To appear in CEUR Workshop Proceedings
summary: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are increasingly used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory (DFT) in high-throughput nanomaterials screening. Systematic softening has been reported for several universal MLIPs when high-energy and far-from-equilibrium configurations are underrepresented in training data. We examine how this behavior appears at under-coordinated edge sites in graphene quantum dots (GQDs), where a vacancy can have pronounced molecular-radical character. Using coronene (C$_{24}$H$_{12}$), a hexagonal GQD with $D_{6h}$ symmetry and three carbon classes, we benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT (GPAW) for monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone-Wales defects. Beyond the full site- and bond-resolved landscapes, we perform a controlled matched-reconstruction comparison in which 28 vacancy and divacancy configurations are scored by both engines using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs. In this dataset, SevenNet underestimates all 28 vacancy and divacancy formation energies, and the mean deficit increases with under-coordination within each defect family: 0.30-0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65-1.11 eV for divacancies as the number of broken edge C-H bonds increases. By contrast, the mean Stone-Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV. SevenNet also preserves the ordering of three hydrogen-dependent reconstruction basins and reproduces $D_{6h}$-equivalent sites to within a few meV. The within-class symmetry spread therefore provides a practical diagnostic of basin-sensitive relaxations. Within the present coronene benchmark, these results support MLIP-based structure screening and preliminary ranking, while absolute vacancy energies and multi-basin edge configurations still require DFT validation.

title: Shallow water equations on n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds: a kinetic approach
summary: We develop an intrinsic kinetic moment closure for shallow-water equations on smooth manifolds of arbitrary dimension equipped with prescribed, possibly time-dependent Riemannian metrics. Hamiltonian transport on the cotangent bundle and metric-dependent momentum integration yield balance laws with hydrostatic pressure, bottom topography, a skew-adjoint force, and dissipative bottom friction. An explicit compactly supported Gibbs equilibrium satisfies the required mass, momentum, and tensor second-moment conditions. We derive the quasilinear formulation and characteristic speeds, establish the continuous mechanical-energy balance with geometric work and frictional dissipation, and obtain a weak entropy inequality for vanishing-viscosity limits under stated convergence assumptions. On the rotating sphere with a fixed round metric, the skew-adjoint force represents Coriolis effects. We construct a kinetic finite-volume scheme combining local fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, and geometric source terms. A second-order time integrator uses independently restricted steps at its two Euler stages. The scheme conserves discrete water volume, preserves nonnegative depth under a sufficient CFL condition, and is well balanced for lakes at rest, including wet/dry interfaces. Six-hour simulations of a localized surface disturbance over Earth topography with Manning bottom friction maintain positive depths and conserve water volume to near machine precision. Comparison with a spherical central-upwind method shows similar surface-wave propagation and gauge time series, with remaining differences in late-time local extrema.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an intrinsic kinetic moment-closure formulation of shallow-water equations on arbitrary-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, derives energy and entropy properties, and constructs a conservative, positivity-preserving, well-balanced finite-volume scheme, validated on spherical Earth-topography simulations.

A compactly supported Gibbs equilibrium satisfies mass, momentum, and tensor second-moment conditions. The authors derive a quasilinear formulation and characteristic speeds, establish a continuous mechanical-energy balance with geometric work and frictional dissipation, and obtain a weak entropy inequality for vanishing-viscosity limits under stated convergence assumptions. On the rotating sphere with a fixed round metric, the skew-adjoint force represents Coriolis effects. They construct a kinetic finite-volume scheme with local fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, and geometric source terms, using a second-order time integrator with independently restricted steps at its two Euler stages.

title: Chlorophyll-a Fluorescence-Based Optical Temperature Sensor Using Food-Grade Chlorella Extract
summary: This letter reports the development of an optical temperature sensor based on the fluorescence of an extract obtained from \textit{Chlorella}, a unicellular microalga commercially available as food-grade biomass. Using a straightforward ethanolic extraction route, the sensing platform exploits the characteristic emission of chlorophyll-\textit{a} as the optical transducing parameter. The operating principle relies on thermal fluorescence quenching, which promotes a decrease in emission intensity with rising temperature. In the temperature range from $28.6$ to $43.0~^{\circ}\text{C}$, the sensor exhibited a linear response ($R^2 = 0.9963$) with a sensitivity of $(-8.9 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-3}~^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$. Dynamic testing over consecutive heating--cooling cycles confirmed the sensor operation under sub-degree thermal oscillations and enabled the characterization of the system's photobleaching drift ($3.65\%\cdot\text{h}^{-1}$). The results reported herein demonstrate the feasibility of exploiting sustainable, bio-derived microalgal pigments as functional photoactive materials for optical thermometry.

AI.tldr: A simple optical temperature sensor was made from a food-grade Chlorella extract, using chlorophyll-a fluorescence quenching as the temperature signal. It showed a linear response from 28.6 to 43.0 °C, sensitivity of (-8.9 ± 0.2) × 10^-3 °C^-1, sub-degree thermal resolution in dynamic tests, and measurable photobleaching drift.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to demonstrate the feasibility of using sustainable, bio-derived microalgal pigments as functional photoactive materials for optical thermometry, leveraging commercially available food-grade Chlorella biomass and a straightforward extraction route.
AI.method: Chlorophyll-a was obtained from Chlorella via ethanolic extraction, and its characteristic fluorescence emission was used as the optical transduction parameter. The sensor relies on thermal fluorescence quenching, in which emission intensity decreases with rising temperature. Performance was tested from 28.6 to 43.0 °C and over consecutive heating–cooling cycles, including characterization of photobleaching drift.
AI.result: The sensor exhibited a linear response with R^2 = 0.9963 and a sensitivity of (-8.9 ± 0.2) × 10^-3 °C^-1 over 28.6–43.0 °C. Dynamic testing confirmed operation under sub-degree thermal oscillations and showed a photobleaching drift of 3.65%·h^-1.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate the feasibility of exploiting sustainable, bio-derived microalgal pigments as functional photoactive materials for optical thermometry.

title: SFQED Cascade Saturation and Laser Depletion Dynamics In CP Rotating Laser Standing Waves
summary: Multi-petawatt laser facilities are approaching the regime where colliding laser pulses can spontaneously ignite self-sustained QED cascades, converting laser energy into dense electron-positron plasmas. Using 1D PIC-QED simulations of a circularly polarized standing wave, we characterize the complete lifecycle of seeded cascades from exponential growth through relativistic opacity and macroscopic laser depletion. We show that cascade saturation is governed by the competition between pair creation and longitudinal lepton migration out of the magnetic nodes. The overdense plasma reflects the driving laser, disrupting the standing wave and triggering secondary cascades in adjacent nodes, driving an apparent spatial expansion whose velocity scales linearly with the cascade growth rate. Finally, we generalize an analytical laser absorption model to realistic time-dependent pulse envelopes, accurately reproducing the simulated conversion efficiency of laser energy into gamma-ray photons and electron-positron pairs.

AI.tldr: 1D PIC-QED simulations show that seeded QED cascades in a circularly polarized laser standing wave saturate through competition between pair creation and longitudinal lepton migration, then deplete the laser via overdense-plasma reflection and secondary cascades; a generalized absorption model reproduces the energy conversion.
AI.motivation: Multi-petawatt laser facilities are approaching the regime where colliding pulses can spontaneously ignite self-sustained QED cascades, converting laser energy into dense electron-positron plasmas, so the cascade lifecycle, saturation, laser depletion, and energy conversion need to be characterized.
AI.method: The authors use 1D PIC-QED simulations of a circularly polarized standing wave with seeded cascades and generalize an analytical laser absorption model to realistic time-dependent pulse envelopes.
AI.result: Cascade saturation is governed by competition between pair creation and longitudinal lepton migration out of the magnetic nodes. The overdense plasma reflects the driving laser, disrupts the standing wave, triggers secondary cascades in adjacent nodes, and drives an apparent spatial expansion whose velocity scales linearly with the cascade growth rate. The generalized absorption model accurately reproduces the simulated conversion efficiency of laser energy into gamma-ray photons and electron-positron pairs.
AI.conclusion: The paper characterizes the complete seeded-cascade lifecycle from exponential growth through relativistic opacity to macroscopic laser depletion, explains saturation and secondary-cascade expansion, and provides a validated absorption framework for realistic pulse envelopes.

title: TARANG: an open-source, cost-controlled design workflow for silicon nitride microcomb chips
summary: Designing a microresonator frequency comb chip means solving a chain of coupled problems: a waveguide with anomalous dispersion that survives fabrication errors, a ring with the right free spectral range and quality factor, a bus gap that sets the coupling regime, and grating couplers, all made in one lithography step. We present TARANG, an open-source Python package that takes a silicon nitride platform from tabulated refractive indices to a GDSII mask in fourteen stages, built on the Tidy3D mode, FDTD and eigenmode-expansion solvers. Every cloud simulation is priced before it runs and capped, every result is cached by a fingerprint of the full simulation, and every quoted number carries a numerical check. We show that snapping the grid onto the core's faces, a common way to steady dispersion calculations, leaves the field samples on the faces to floating-point rounding, and that averaging solves with the grid just inside and just outside the faces makes the group-velocity dispersion $D$ independent of the computer and steady to about 1 ps/(nm km) from mesh to mesh. Two complete air-clad designs are presented, at 1550 nm ($700\times1000$ nm core, $D = 372.9 \pm 0.6$ ps/(nm km)) and at 780 nm ($350\times500$ nm, $D = 196.4 \pm 0.9$ ps/(nm km)), each with a 200 GHz ring, critical and over-coupled gaps, grating couplers, and a fibre-to-fibre budget. The predicted dispersion agrees with two measured devices from the literature to within 1 and 4%, and an independent Lugiato-Lefever solver forms stable single solitons from the exported parameters of both designs, which are ready for fabrication.

AI.tldr: TARANG is an open-source Python workflow that designs silicon nitride microresonator frequency-comb chips in fourteen stages, from material indices to GDSII, with cost-capped cloud simulations, caching, and numerical checks. It introduces a face-grid averaging method for stable dispersion calculations and demonstrates two fabrication-ready air-clad designs at 1550 nm and 780 nm.
AI.motivation: Microcomb chip design requires jointly solving coupled waveguide dispersion, ring geometry, quality factor, bus coupling, and grating coupler problems in a single lithography step. The authors aim to provide a cost-controlled, reproducible, open-source workflow that makes this chain tractable and numerically reliable.
AI.method: The paper presents TARANG, an open-source Python package built on Tidy3D mode, FDTD, and eigenmode-expansion solvers. It implements a fourteen-stage silicon nitride design flow from tabulated refractive indices to GDSII, prices and caps every cloud simulation before execution, caches results using full-simulation fingerprints, and attaches numerical checks to quoted values. It also compares grid-snapping with averaging simulations placed just inside and outside core faces to stabilize group-velocity dispersion.
AI.result: The workflow produces two complete air-clad designs: a 1550 nm design with a 700×1000 nm core and D = 372.9 ± 0.6 ps/(nm km), and a 780 nm design with a 350×500 nm core and D = 196.4 ± 0.9 ps/(nm km). Each includes a 200 GHz ring, critical and over-coupled gaps, grating couplers, and a fibre-to-fibre budget. AI.conclusion: TARANG enables cost-controlled, reproducible silicon nitride microcomb chip design and yields two fabrication-ready designs validated by literature dispersion comparisons and independent soliton simulations. Its face-grid averaging procedure improves the robustness of dispersion calculations relative to grid snapping.

title: Lifetime of localized turbulence in transitional channel flow
summary: The lifetime of localized turbulence in transitional channel flow, the so-called turbulent stripes or bands, as a function of the Reynolds number ($Re$) is reported here. Recent studies showed that although the mean lifetime of a turbulent band increases with the band length, it appears to saturate at a certain critical length, which is smaller than the fully developed band length. However, this observation was based on a single Reynolds number only. Here, we first confirmed this saturation by considering higher Reynolds numbers. This property enables us to measure the characteristic lifetime of a turbulent band without having to resolve it at its full length, which greatly reduces the computational cost and makes statistical studies by direct numerical simulation (DNS) feasible near the lower end of the transitional-$Re$ regime. Subsequently, by extensive DNS, we measured the lifetime up to $Re=670$, and the data cover more than two orders of magnitude, ranging from $O(10^2)$ to nearly $O(10^5)$ and revealing a sharp but smooth growth with increasing $Re$. No sudden divergence of the lifetime was observed in the $Re$ range investigated, in which controversy existed over whether or not a turbulent band would become sustained. Despite significant differences between the structure and dynamics of channel bands and pipe puffs, our data concretely support a unified transition scenario in the two flows.

AI.tldr: Extensive direct numerical simulations show that the lifetime of localized turbulent bands in transitional channel flow increases sharply but smoothly with Reynolds number up to 670, with no sudden divergence, supporting a unified transition scenario with pipe puffs.
AI.motivation: Previous evidence that turbulent-band mean lifetime saturates with band length was based on a single Reynolds number, and controversy remained over whether turbulent bands become sustained. Resolving full-length bands is computationally expensive.
AI.method: The study confirmed lifetime saturation at higher Reynolds numbers, exploited this property to measure characteristic band lifetime without resolving the full band length, and performed extensive direct numerical simulations up to Reynolds number 670.
AI.result: The measured lifetimes span more than two orders of magnitude, from O(10^2) to nearly O(10^5), and grow sharply but smoothly with Reynolds number. No sudden divergence of lifetime was observed in the investigated range.
AI.conclusion: No evidence of sudden lifetime divergence was found up to Reynolds number 670. Despite structural and dynamical differences between channel bands and pipe puffs, the data support a unified transition scenario for the two flows.

title: Inverse Design of an On-chip Phase-Change Switch Composed of Sparse Heterogeneous Metasurfaces
summary: Photonic switches are exploited for optical signal routing and control within optical communication systems. The integration of phase change materials with silicon photonic switches overcomes the drawbacks of the state-of-the-art photonic switches based on electro-optic and thermo-optic effects. In this work, a 1x2 on-chip switch with a footprint of 6.3umx31um based on on-chip one-dimensional metasurfaces is inverse-designed. The on-chip metasurfaces are heterogeneous, which their meta-atoms can be composed of either SiO2 or the phase-change material Sb2Se3. This helps to the realization of higher extinction ratio between the switch outputs, especially at the amorphous state which has a small refractive index contrast to that of the silicon. To benefit from structural, fabrication and switching simplicity, sparse parameterization is followed in the inverse design of the switch using ternary search (TS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms.

AI.tldr: This paper inverse-designs a compact 1x2 on-chip photonic switch using sparse heterogeneous one-dimensional metasurfaces whose meta-atoms are made of SiO2 or the phase-change material Sb2Se3, with ternary search and particle swarm optimization used for sparse parameterization.
AI.motivation: Photonic switches are needed for optical signal routing and control in optical communication systems, and phase-change materials combined with silicon photonics can overcome drawbacks of electro-optic and thermo-optic photonic switches.
AI.method: A 1x2 on-chip switch with a 6.3 um x 31 um footprint is inverse-designed from heterogeneous on-chip one-dimensional metasurfaces, where each meta-atom can be SiO2 or Sb2Se3. Sparse parameterization is used with ternary search and particle swarm optimization to simplify structure, fabrication, and switching.
AI.result: The heterogeneous metasurface design is intended to increase the extinction ratio between switch outputs, particularly in the amorphous state where the refractive-index contrast with silicon is small. Quantitative extinction ratio, insertion loss, and switching-speed values are not provided in the abstract.

title: Impurity turbulent transport and its role in driving zonal flows in tokamak plasmas
summary: The driving mechanisms of zonal flows (ZFs) in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas are investigated by using gyrokinetic theory and simulations. For deuterium plasmas containing either helium ash with a steep density gradient or lithium impurity at a high charge concentration, the magnitude of impurity turbulent energy flux (TEF) can be comparable to, or even stronger than, that of the main-ion TEF. Moreover, the impurity TEF significantly drives ZFs. Both the impurity and main-ion turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress (PRS) drives are significant for the case with a high lithium charge concentration. The shielding timescale of the turbulent PRS drive is found to be the damping time of geodesic acoustic mode, which is significantly shorter than one ion bounce period.

AI.tldr: Gyrokinetic theory and simulations show that in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas, impurity turbulent energy fluxes can rival or exceed main-ion fluxes and significantly drive zonal flows; turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress drives and their shielding by geodesic acoustic mode damping are also analyzed.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to clarify the driving mechanisms of zonal flows in tokamak plasmas containing multiple ion species, including impurities.
AI.method: The authors use gyrokinetic theory and simulations for deuterium plasmas with either helium ash having a steep density gradient or lithium impurity at high charge concentration.
AI.result: Impurity turbulent energy flux can be comparable to or stronger than main-ion turbulent energy flux and significantly drives zonal flows. Both impurity and main-ion turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress drives are significant at high lithium charge concentration. The shielding timescale of the turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress drive equals the geodesic acoustic mode damping time and is much shorter than one ion bounce period.
AI.conclusion: Impurity turbulent transport is an important zonal-flow drive in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas, and poloidal Reynolds stress shielding is governed by geodesic acoustic mode damping rather than the ion bounce timescale.

title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
summary: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) builds zero-point energy and tunnelling into classical trajectories and is widely used for bimolecular rate coefficients. At low temperature it requires many beads, and the stiff ring-polymer springs then limit the integrator. The Cayley modification of the free ring-polymer step removes this limit, but it has so far been formulated mode by mode, which requires Fourier transforms of every degree of freedom at every step. Here we show that, in bead coordinates, the Cayley step reduces to one cyclic tridiagonal solve for the midpoint of the step, with a matrix that depends only on the number of beads $P$, the temperature and the time step, and not on the atomic masses. The bead-space step is exactly the normal-mode Cayley map: it conserves the free ring-polymer energy, preserves the free ring-polymer Boltzmann distribution, and is stable for any $P$ whenever $ΩΔt<2$ for the highest physical frequency $Ω$. A Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction solves it in about $18P$ operations per degree of freedom without pivoting, with a condition number bounded by $1+(ω_PΔt)^2$, and the inverse matrix decays geometrically with bead separation, so the step is local in bead index. Implemented in the open-source PyRPMD package, the propagator reproduces normal-mode Cayley to $1.5\times10^{-15}$ for up to 2048 beads and its cost grows linearly with $P$. For direct RPMD (dRPMD), which has so far integrated the springs explicitly, these properties raise the stability limit on the time step 23--29-fold in published low-temperature settings; at \SI{20}{K} with 3072 beads, the Cayley step conserves the ring-polymer energy as well as velocity Verlet does with a time step about ten times larger, while leaving the low-lying internal modes that govern spurious resonances essentially unchanged.

AI.tldr: A bead-space Cayley propagator for ring-polymer molecular dynamics avoids per-step Fourier transforms by reducing the free ring-polymer step to a cyclic tridiagonal solve, giving an exact, stable, local, linear-scaling integrator that improves direct RPMD time-step stability.
AI.motivation: Low-temperature RPMD requires many beads, and the resulting stiff ring-polymer springs limit the integrator. The Cayley modification removes this limit but has been formulated mode by mode, requiring Fourier transforms of every degree of freedom at every step.
AI.method: The authors formulate the Cayley step in bead coordinates as one cyclic tridiagonal solve for the midpoint of the step, with a matrix depending only on bead number P, temperature, and time step, not atomic masses. They solve it with a Thomas recursion plus a rank-two Woodbury correction without pivoting, analyze its conservation, distribution, stability, conditioning, and locality properties, implement it in PyRPMD, compare it with normal-mode Cayley, and test it in direct RPMD.

AI.conclusion: The bead-space Cayley propagator provides an exact, stable, local, and linear-scaling alternative to Fourier-transform-based normal-mode Cayley integration for RPMD and improves direct RPMD stability without materially altering the low-frequency internal modes that govern spurious resonances.

title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
summary: Linear stability analysis of compressible shear flows beyond continuum regime attracts increasing attention in recent years accounting for high-altitude applications. In this paper, the temporal stability of high-speed plane Couette flow in near-continuum regime is addressed. A novel linear stability method based on the generalized hydrodynamic equations (GHE) with slip boundary conditions is developed within the 13-moment framework. Meanwhile, the linear stability equations of the nonlinear coupled constitutive relations (NCCR) and the Navier--Stokes (NS) equations are also given. Based on the developed methods, the linear stability of plane Couette flows at $Ma=2.5$--10 and $Kn=2.7\times 10^{-5}$--0.07 are analyzed, and the rarefaction effects on the base flow, eigenspectrum, mode synchronization and least stable mode are investigated. The results show that the GHE with slip boundary conditions agrees well with direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) results in predicting base flow profiles of velocity, temperature, all stress and heat flux components, while the NS equations show considerable differences, especially for capturing the nonlinear normal stress and tangential heat flux. The GHE-based linear stability theory (LST) recovers to the classical NS-based LST in the continuum limit, while they show considerable differences when $Kn$ reaches $O(0.01)$. As rarefaction degree increases, the synchronization between acoustic modes and viscous modes becomes weak, and all modes become stable in rarefied plane Couette flow. The surface slip effect and nonlinear transport increase the disturbance phase speeds, while they have different effects on the growth rate of different modes. Generally, rarefaction effects increase the growth rate of the least stable Mode II at low wavenumbers, and show more pronounced effects on higher modes and high-wavenumber disturbances.

AI.tldr: A linear stability method using generalized hydrodynamic equations with slip boundary conditions is developed for high-speed plane Couette flow in the near-continuum regime, and rarefaction effects on base flow and stability are analyzed for Ma=2.5–10 and Kn=2.7×10^-5–0.07.
AI.motivation: High-altitude applications motivate linear stability analysis of compressible shear flows beyond the continuum regime, particularly near-continuum high-speed plane Couette flow where rarefaction effects may invalidate classical Navier–Stokes descriptions.

AI.conclusion: The GHE-based linear stability theory provides a more appropriate near-continuum description than Navier–Stokes for high-speed plane Couette flow, and rarefaction, slip, and nonlinear transport effects are important for stability predictions beyond the continuum regime.

title: Ultracompact and Nonvolatile On-chip Switch Based on DBS and PSO Algorithms
summary: A 1x2 photonic switch based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI)-Sb2Se3 hybrid platform is inverse-designed using direct binary search (DBS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms. The nonvolatile on-chip switch is designed to consist of minimum switchable phase-change units and operates based on the en-masse switching of all Sb2Se3 cells from crystalline to amorphous and vice-versa. The device has a small footprint of only 6.3umx31um. At the wavelength of 1550nm, it exhibits an insertion loss of less than 0.96dB, and its crosstalk is measured to be less than -12dB within the three-dimensional (3D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations.

AI.tldr: An inverse-designed 1×2 nonvolatile SOI–Sb2Se3 photonic switch using DBS and PSO achieves a 6.3×31 µm footprint, <0.96 dB insertion loss, and <-12 dB crosstalk at 1550 nm in 3D FDTD simulations.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to realize an ultracompact, nonvolatile on-chip photonic switch using a silicon-on-insulator–Sb2Se3 hybrid platform and inverse design.
AI.method: A 1×2 photonic switch is inverse-designed with direct binary search (DBS) and particle swarm optimization (PSO). The device uses minimum switchable phase-change units and operates by en-masse switching of all Sb2Se3 cells between crystalline and amorphous states; performance is evaluated with three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations.
AI.result: The switch has a footprint of 6.3 µm × 31 µm. At 1550 nm, it exhibits insertion loss below 0.96 dB and crosstalk below -12 dB in 3D FDTD simulations.
AI.conclusion: DBS/PSO inverse design enables an ultracompact nonvolatile on-chip switch based on en-masse Sb2Se3 phase switching with low insertion loss and crosstalk; the abstract does not provide fabrication or experimental validation details.

title: Cross-channel amplification of frequency-distinct scattered waves in multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering
summary: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) can be amplified when one side-scattered wave draws energy from several pumps, each through a separate ion-acoustic-wave (IAW) branch. This is not common-daughter-wave coupling: scattered waves from different parent pumps may occupy nearly the same wave-vector region yet remain distinct optical modes because their frequencies differ. We examine this process with local-growth and finite-width-gain models, three-dimensional coupled-mode calculations and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. Adding the extra branches increases temporal growth and spatial gain across the tested crossing angles. In three dimensions, direct branches alone give weak, localized side scatter; with the cross branches present, a strong field fills much of the interaction region even though the incident beams, direct channels and initial seed are unchanged. The distinction persists at fixed total power. The coupled response remains strong as the power per beam falls, whereas the direct-only response drops rapidly. PIC spectra contain nearby scattered-light features accompanied by several pump-specific IAW branches, and the fixed-power scans yield a strong, non-monotonic response. These results support cross-channel feedback through separate IAWs as a multibeam SBS amplification mechanism that may help predict and control SBS losses in laser-fusion plasmas.

AI.tldr: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering can amplify frequency-distinct side-scattered waves through separate ion-acoustic-wave branches from different pumps, producing stronger and more spatially extended coupling than direct channels alone in models and PIC simulations.
AI.motivation: The paper examines a multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering process in which one side-scattered wave draws energy from several pumps through separate ion-acoustic-wave branches, rather than through common-daughter-wave coupling. The authors aim to identify a multibeam SBS amplification mechanism that may help predict and control SBS losses in laser-fusion plasmas.
AI.method: The study uses local-growth and finite-width-gain models, three-dimensional coupled-mode calculations, and two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations. It compares direct branches with cross branches across tested crossing angles, at fixed total power, and as power per beam falls; PIC spectra are also analyzed for scattered-light features and pump-specific ion-acoustic-wave branches. Exact simulation parameters and quantitative gain values are not provided in the abstract.
AI.result: Adding extra ion-acoustic-wave branches increases temporal growth and spatial gain across the tested crossing angles. In three dimensions, direct branches alone produce weak, localized side scatter, whereas with cross branches present a strong field fills much of the interaction region even though the incident beams, direct channels, and initial seed are unchanged. title: A thermodynamically consistent, fully compressible, fluctuating hydrodynamics model of a Cahn Hilliard binary fluid mixture
summary: We derive, from first principles, a thermodynamically consistent set of fully compressible fluctuating hydrodynamic equations for a Cahn-Hilliard binary fluid mixture, in isothermal and non-isothermal form and for symmetric and non-symmetric mixtures. The derivation uses the GENERIC formalism, with the friction operator constructed from flux fluctuations following Jelic and Ottinger, so that deterministic and stochastic fluxes derive from the same operator and correlation matrix and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem holds by construction. We show that the momentum equation must use the total mass density, that the Cahn-Hilliard variable is the mass fraction, and that the diffusion flux must be driven by the specific, not the volumetric, exchange potential. We derive a generalized Korteweg tensor for square-gradient energies in density and composition, and show that the reversible pressure tensor of the non-isothermal model is fixed by the degeneracy condition, producing a thermal capillary stress when the interfacial free energy has an entropic part. Thermodynamic consistency is proved in full: Jacobi identity, positivity and degeneracy, local energy conservation with interstitial-working fluxes, a local entropy balance, Soret-Dufour reciprocity, and Einstein statistics of the linearized equations. The final equations are written in conservative form for finite-volume discretization, and closed-form static and dynamic structure factors are given for all models as analytic benchmarks. An appendix shows that the same models follow from classical irreversible thermodynamics with the Helmholtz or Gibbs free energy; this route is unique for isothermal flows and has a gauge freedom in the non-isothermal case that GENERIC removes.

AI.conclusion: A thermodynamically consistent, fully compressible, fluctuating hydrodynamic model of Cahn-Hilliard binary fluid mixtures is established, written in conservative form suitable for finite-volume discretization, validated against analytic structure-factor benchmarks, and shown to be equivalent to a classical irreversible thermodynamics derivation up to a non-isothermal gauge freedom eliminated by the GENERIC construction.

title: Generative AI models for exploring diffusion dynamics from multi-frame particle tracking
summary: Particle-based volumetric flow measurement techniques have proven their efficacy in quantitatively assessing the dynamic characteristics of unsteady flows within the realm of fluid mechanics. Despite recent advances in multi-frame particle tracking, an open challenge in this area is maintaining trajectories in temporally under-sampled 3D sequences, where inter-frame displacements are large. In this work, we develop DiffTR-Flow3D, a diffusion-based model that estimates flow motion from spatiotemporal three-dimensional particle recordings via a stochastic diffusion process. DiffTR-Flow3D conditions the diffusion process with both global and local particle dynamics and enhances flow estimation by leveraging historical particle trajectories. Extensive experiments, including numerical simulations and real-world measurements, demonstrate that DiffTR-Flow3D achieves state-of-the-art displacement estimation accuracy compared with learning-based flow estimators, and, when integrated into particle tracking pipelines, substantially improves their long-term tracking performance, while exhibiting robustness and generalization across diverse flow patterns. This work is expected to provide fluid researchers with an effective tool for the consistent and precise analysis of particle trajectories in temporally under-sampled 3D sequences with large inter-frame displacements.

AI.tldr: DiffTR-Flow3D is a diffusion-based flow estimator that uses global and local particle dynamics plus historical trajectories to improve displacement estimation and long-term tracking in temporally under-sampled 3D particle sequences with large inter-frame displacements.
AI.motivation: Multi-frame particle tracking enables quantitative analysis of unsteady volumetric flows, but maintaining trajectories remains challenging when 3D sequences are temporally under-sampled and inter-frame displacements are large.
AI.method: The authors develop DiffTR-Flow3D, a stochastic diffusion model that estimates flow motion from spatiotemporal 3D particle recordings, conditioned on both global and local particle dynamics and enhanced by historical particle trajectories.
AI.result: Extensive numerical simulations and real-world measurements show state-of-the-art displacement estimation accuracy compared with learning-based flow estimators, substantially improved long-term tracking when integrated into particle tracking pipelines, and robustness and generalization across diverse flow patterns.
AI.conclusion: DiffTR-Flow3D is expected to provide fluid researchers with an effective tool for consistent and precise analysis of particle trajectories in temporally under-sampled 3D sequences with large inter-frame displacements.

title: Enabling Mie Resonances for Optomagnetism in Epitaxially Grown Garnet Nanodisks via Photonic Crystals
summary: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate compatible with epitaxial growth on gadolinium gallium garnet is proposed for controlling the optomagnetic response of a single bismuth iron garnet nanodisk. The photonic environment modifies the spectral positions and relative strengths of the electric- and magnetic-dipole contributions and redistributes the optical field inside the disk. Compared with a reference nanodisk on a homogeneous substrate evaluated near the broad maximum of its summed multipolar response, the peak axial optical contribution to the inverse Faraday effect in the examined cross-sections is enhanced by factors of approximately 7.3 and 6.3 in the magnetic- and electric-dipole-dominated regimes, respectively. The enhancement reaches approximately 7.9 at the maximum of the summed multipolar scattering contributions. These results demonstrate spectral control of the magnitude and spatial distribution of the local optomagnetic response through the photonic environment, without changing the nanodisk geometry.

AI.tldr: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate is used to tune the Mie resonances of a single epitaxial bismuth iron garnet nanodisk, enhancing the local optomagnetic (inverse Faraday) response by up to ~7.9x without altering the disk geometry.
AI.motivation: The optomagnetic response of a single garnet nanodisk is governed by its electric- and magnetic-dipole Mie resonances, which are fixed by geometry; the authors aim to show that the surrounding photonic environment can instead be used to control the spectral position, relative strength, and spatial distribution of that response.
AI.method: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate compatible with epitaxial growth on gadolinium gallium garnet is proposed and used to modify the photonic environment of a single bismuth iron garnet nanodisk. The multipolar (electric- and magnetic-dipole) contributions and the internal optical field distribution are analyzed and compared with a reference nanodisk on a homogeneous substrate, evaluating the axial optical contribution to the inverse Faraday effect and the summed multipolar response.
