title: Multi-dimensional kinetic modeling of laser-plasma instabilities by a Vlasov-Maxwell system
summary: We present PLAW-EM2d (Two-Dimensional PLAsmaWave ElectroMagnetic Simulation), a two-dimensional Vlasov-Maxwell code for kinetic studies of laser-plasma interactions. The code combines a hybrid electrostatic- TEz field decomposition with an Eulerian 2d2v Vlasov solver for the electron distribution function and a cold closure for the out-of-plane response. Vacuum propagation, Landau damping, and a homogeneousplasma comparison with PIC simulations benchmark the coupled solver. We then consider two representative SRS problems. In an inhomogeneous plasma, the code reproduces convective SRS backscatter with a reflectivity consistent with the Rosenbluth estimate. In a transversely extended target, it captures SRS side scattering in a self-consistent two-dimensional Vlasov simulation, resolving oblique electromagnetic and Langmuir waves that satisfy the resonance conditions. These calculations show that PLAW-EM2d can describe both conventional SRS backscatter and a two-dimensional side-scattering channel relevant to laser-plasma interactions in ICF.

AI.motivation: The work is motivated by the need for multi-dimensional kinetic modeling of laser-plasma instabilities, with attention to both conventional stimulated Raman scattering backscatter and side-scattering channels relevant to laser-plasma interactions in inertial confinement fusion.

title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
summary: Turbulence modeling relies on human choices of closure form, physical inputs, and tunable parameters. Training closures a posteriori is efficient only with gradients through long chaotic rollouts, which few solvers provide. Most a posteriori approaches therefore resort to gradient-free optimization, and nearly all fix the closure form in advance, learning only its parameters. In this work, we introduce a gradient-aware agentic framework that poses closure discovery as a bilevel problem: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system searches over closure forms, while a GPU-native differentiable computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver supplies gradients, making differentiable a posteriori learning an action of the autonomous AI agent. For each proposal, the agents construct a differentiable training program by embedding the analytical, neural, or hybrid closure in the solver, implementing a differentiable objective, and validating the gradient path. They then decide whether to evaluate the closure, compute its parameter sensitivities, or train it a posteriori, select the optimization settings, and revise subsequent proposals using the simulation outcomes and returned gradients. Truncated-horizon gradients make this training usable under chaotic dynamics for closures with tens of thousands of parameters. Demonstrations include dissipation-law and subgrid-scale closure discovery in two-dimensional turbulence and wall-model discovery for large-eddy simulation of three-dimensional channel flow. With gradient-based training, the agent recovers reference coefficients that forward evaluation alone does not reach within the same budget, and autonomously discovers and trains analytical and neural closures that improve agreement with the targeted reference statistics. These results demonstrate the feasibility of end-to-end autonomous turbulence model development in time-resolved flows.

title: Three-body streaming forces lower the axial binding threshold of a held transverse three-sphere chain
summary: Particles in oscillatory liquids can form chains perpendicular to the drive. We ask whether the forces between isolated pairs predict when three spheres can bind at a finite spacing. We first hold the spheres fixed during small-amplitude oscillation and calculate the cycle-averaged force on an end sphere. The three-body contribution lowers the critical Stokes number from 4.283 for the pair-additive model to 3.534 for the full chain, a reduction of 17.5 percent. An independent finite-element calculation reproduces the shift. The three-body attraction also draws the spheres close enough for the nearest-neighbour pair forces to become repulsive. This compression accounts for most of the tendency to bend out of the plane containing the drive and the chain. For freely translating and rotating spheres at a particle-to-liquid density ratio of 2.2, the multipole calculation predicts initial growth of this bend at five sampled equilibria. A point-singularity calculation confirms the sign at two of those spacings.

AI.tldr: Three-body streaming forces in an oscillatory liquid lower the axial binding threshold for a held transverse three-sphere chain, reducing the critical Stokes number by 17.5% relative to a pair-additive model and promoting out-of-plane bending.
AI.motivation: The paper asks whether forces between isolated particle pairs are sufficient to predict when three spheres in an oscillatory liquid can bind at a finite spacing, or whether three-body contributions qualitatively and quantitatively change the binding threshold.
AI.method: The authors hold three spheres fixed under small-amplitude oscillation and compute the cycle-averaged force on an end sphere, comparing a pair-additive model with the full three-body chain and validating the shift with an independent finite-element calculation. They also use multipole calculations for freely translating and rotating spheres at a particle-to-liquid density ratio of 2.2, with a point-singularity calculation used as a check.
AI.result: The three-body contribution lowers the critical Stokes number from 4.283 in the pair-additive model to 3.534 for the full chain, a 17.5% reduction, and the finite-element calculation reproduces this shift. The three-body attraction compresses the chain enough that nearest-neighbour pair forces become repulsive; this compression accounts for most of the tendency to bend out of the plane containing the drive and the chain. AI.conclusion: Pair-additive forces are insufficient to predict the axial binding threshold of the three-sphere chain. Three-body streaming forces materially lower the threshold, induce compression and pair repulsion, and drive an out-of-plane bending tendency that is predicted to grow for freely translating and rotating spheres.

title: Chiral high harmonic generation via coherent superposition of multi-channel interband transitions
summary: Circularly polarized light, with its specific handedness, is a valuable tool for investigating the chirality related properties of materials, including their structural, electronic, magnetic and topological characteristics. This has led to efforts in creating wavelength-tunable coherent light with circular or elliptical polarization through a sub-cycle ultrafast process high-harmonic generation (HHG). Existing approaches to chiral HHG, however, typically rely on multidimensional driving fields, materials engineering or complex optical architectures. Here we uncover a distinct mechanism without such complexity, where a single linearly polarized driving field generates chiral HHG from a pristine crystal. We show that, in the Weyl semimetal NbP, one linearly polarized near-infrared driving field generates high harmonics with pronounced ellipticity. Semi-conductor Bloch equations (SBEs) reveal that this ellipticity originates from the coherent superposition of multiple interband transitions, each contributing harmonics with distinct linear polarizations and relative phases. We further substantiate this mechanism by shifting the driving photon energy into the mid-infrared, which strongly suppresses the ellipticity as the number of accessible interband transition channels is reduced. These results establish a simple and general mechanism for chiral HHG, and show that quantum materials can transform an apparently achiral driving field into polarization-tunable ultrafast chiral emission.

Existing chiral HHG approaches typically require multidimensional driving fields, materials engineering, or complex optical architectures, motivating a simpler mechanism.
AI.method: The authors use a single linearly polarized near-infrared driving field on pristine Weyl semimetal NbP and analyze the polarization of the generated high harmonics. Semiconductor Bloch equations are used to identify the contributions of multiple interband transitions, and the driving photon energy is shifted to the mid-infrared to test the role of accessible interband transition channels.

title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
summary: Opacity of mid- and high-$Z$ plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly \emph{which} fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to $K$ \emph{non-contiguous} groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5\% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of $K$ uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of $4\times10^{15}$--$1.1\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-3}$, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900$\um$, the model with $K=100$ reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2\% and a 90th-percentile error of 8\%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

For a Sn plasma, K=100 reproduces a 1500-group reference flux with 2% median error and 8% 90th-percentile error, ten times better than a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

title: Efficient refractive-index sweeps in the discrete dipole approximation using shifted Krylov methods
summary: The discrete dipole approximation (DDA) is a flexible numerical method for simulating electromagnetic scattering by particles of arbitrary shape and internal structure. In many applications, such as optical-database generation, the same particle geometry must be simulated for many values of the complex refractive index, which are currently handled independently with proportional increase of computational time. For homogeneous particles, however, variations of the refractive index affect only the diagonal polarizability term of the interaction matrix. The corresponding linear systems therefore differ only by scalar shifts of the identity matrix, making them suitable for shifted Krylov-subspace methods. In this work, we use a shifted Krylov solver adapted to the complex-symmetric formulation of the matrix and implement it in the ADDA code. The method is evaluated for a homogeneous spherical particle over a two-dimensional domain of complex refractive indices. The shifted solver reproduces the extinction cross sections obtained from independent simulations with relative differences below the iterative-method tolerance, while reducing the number of matrix-vector products by a factor of 130 for the tested configuration. We further analyze how the achievable speedup depends on the number of refractive-index values, the computational backend, and the variation of the convergence rate across the parameter space. The final wall-time acceleration for large refractive-index sweeps was demonstrated to be up to 40 times, which can be further improved by optimizing the scattered-fields calculations that became a new bottleneck.

AI.tldr: A shifted Krylov solver is adapted to the complex-symmetric discrete dipole approximation and implemented in ADDA to accelerate electromagnetic scattering simulations over many complex refractive-index values for homogeneous particles.
AI.motivation: In applications such as optical-database generation, the same particle geometry must be simulated for many complex refractive indices, but current DDA workflows treat these independently, increasing computational time proportionally. For homogeneous particles, refractive-index changes affect only the diagonal polarizability term, so the resulting linear systems differ only by scalar shifts of the identity matrix and are suitable for shifted Krylov-subspace methods.

They evaluate it for a homogeneous spherical particle over a two-dimensional domain of complex refractive indices and analyze speedup dependence on the number of refractive-index values, computational backend, and variation in convergence rate across the parameter space.

title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
summary:
We develop two hybrid data-driven Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) Reduced-Order Models (ROMs) for the non-stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations (NSEs) with random viscosity. The proposed framework combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) ROMs, spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and the Stochastic Collocation Method (SCM). A key feature is the approximation of the realization-dependent closure term by the closure associated with the expected viscosity. Consequently, a single data-driven closure model constructed from the full-order solution corresponding to the expected viscosity can be reused across all realizations, thereby avoiding the expensive construction of realization-specific closure models. This leads to the Data-Driven Correction UQ ROM (DDC-UQ-ROM) and its physically constrained variant, the Constrained DDC-UQ-ROM (CDDC-UQ-ROM), in which physical constraints are imposed on the data-driven correction model.
  The proposed methods are evaluated for a two-dimensional (2D) flow past a circular cylinder problem with a 5D random viscosity field, considering mean Reynolds numbers $Re=100$ and $Re=500$, different correlation lengths, and both in-sample and out-of-sample parameter settings. Numerical results show that the DDC-UQ-ROM generally improves upon the standard Galerkin ROM (G-ROM), while the CDDC-UQ-ROM exhibits the most accurate and robust approximation of the benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered. The robustness and accuracy of the CDDC-UQ-ROM are further assessed through statistical error analyses of the first- and second-order energy moments, reduced-training-data experiments, and an indicative comparison of wall-clock computational costs with the full-order UQ calculations.

AI.tldr: The paper develops hybrid POD-based reduced-order UQ models for time-dependent incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with random viscosity, using spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and stochastic collocation. A single closure trained at the expected viscosity is reused across realizations, yielding DDC-UQ-ROM and physically constrained CDDC-UQ-ROM variants. Tests on 2D flow past a cylinder show improved accuracy and robustness, especially for CDDC-UQ-ROM.

In particular, constructing realization-specific data-driven closure models for reduced-order models would be expensive. The work seeks hybrid UQ reduced-order models that retain accuracy while avoiding this per-realization closure construction cost.

The realization-dependent closure term is approximated by the closure associated with the expected viscosity, allowing one data-driven closure model built from the full-order solution at the expected viscosity to be reused across all realizations. This gives the Data-Driven Correction UQ ROM and its physically constrained variant, CDDC-UQ-ROM, where physical constraints are imposed on the data-driven correction. The methods are evaluated on 2D flow past a circular cylinder with a 5D random viscosity field at mean Reynolds numbers Re=100 and Re=500, different correlation lengths, and in-sample and out-of-sample parameter settings.
AI.result: Numerical results show that DDC-UQ-ROM generally improves upon the standard Galerkin ROM, while CDDC-UQ-ROM provides the most accurate and robust approximation of the benchmark energy evolution across the considered cases. Its robustness and accuracy are further assessed through statistical error analyses of first- and second-order energy moments, reduced-training-data experiments, and an indicative comparison of wall-clock computational costs with full-order UQ calculations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid data-driven correction reduced-order stochastic collocation framework is effective for UQ of the time-dependent incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with random viscosity. Reusing a single closure model constructed at the expected viscosity avoids realization-specific closure construction, and the physically constrained CDDC-UQ-ROM is the most accurate and robust variant in the reported tests.

title: Optical fiber shape sensing using picosecond spatiotemporal single-photon reflectometry
comment: Main draft: 24 pages, 8 figures. Supplementary information: 13 pages, 8 figures
summary: Inferring the three-dimensional configuration of a flexible optical fiber from a single accessible end remains a fundamental challenge in photonic sensing. Existing approaches typically require specialised multicore fibers, coherent interferometry, or distributed spectral encoding. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally different sensing paradigm in which fiber geometry is reconstructed from the spatiotemporal dynamics of returning single photons. Using a laser-engineered multimode fiber interrogated by a time-resolved 32x32 single-photon avalanche diode array, we show that fiber deformation imprints unique signatures onto the distribution and arrival time of back-reflected photons. We map these high-dimensional photon-return states onto a low-dimensional geometric manifold, enabling continuous bend-angle estimation and reconstruction of previously unseen two- and three-dimensional shapes from measurements acquired entirely at the proximal fiber end. Measurements show a median pixel-wise signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 26 dB and below 1% repeatability variation. Our results establish multimode single-photon dynamics as an information-rich channel for distributed geometric sensing, introducing a new framework for single-ended fiber shape reconstruction and minimally invasive photonic navigation.

title: Effect of Gas Pressure and Molecular Structure in the Spatial-Mode Conversion of Terahertz Radiation from a Plasma Filament
summary: In this work, the generation of terahertz (THz) radiation under single color filamentation of a femtosecond laser pulse in an optical cell with compressed gases (argon, nitrogen, CO2) in broad pressure range from 0.001 to 25 atm is experimentally studied for the first time. A nonmonotonic dependence of the integral energy of the THz signal on the gas pressure is revealed, which can be attributed to the competition between an increase in the plasma density and the development of plasma selfabsorption processes, multiple filamentation of the femtosecond pump, and collision induced absorption in the neutral medium. We show that the molecular structure of the gas critically determines the pressure optimum of generation, shifting the maximum of the THz energy yield to the region of elevated pressures (from 10 to 15 atm) for monatomic argon and to the region of subatmospheric pressures (approx. 0.1 atm) for molecular carbon dioxide due to strong vibrational rotational dissipation. On the basis of numerical 3D modeling, it is shown that the cylindrical metal waveguide insert used for signal collection operates in a strongly multimode regime and substantially transforms the angular spectrum of the THz source. We demonstrate that the conical structure of the THz radiation recorded in the experiment is a consequence of intermode interference and diffraction at the output end face of the waveguide, which transforms the true parameters of THz generation in the plasma channel.

AI.tldr: Experimental and 3D-modeling study of THz generation by single-color femtosecond laser filamentation in compressed Ar, N2, and CO2 (0.001–25 atm) shows a nonmonotonic pressure dependence, gas-dependent pressure optima, and strong spatial-mode distortion by the multimode collection waveguide.
AI.motivation: To characterize, for the first time over a broad pressure range, how gas pressure and molecular structure affect THz generation from a laser-produced plasma filament and to determine whether the measured THz spatial structure represents the source or is altered by the collection waveguide.
AI.method: Single-color femtosecond-laser filamentation in an optical cell filled with compressed argon, nitrogen, or CO2 at 0.001–25 atm; measurement of integral THz energy versus pressure; and numerical 3D modeling of the cylindrical metal waveguide insert and its multimode angular-spectrum transformation.
AI.result: THz energy depended nonmonotonically on pressure because plasma-density growth competed with plasma self-absorption, multiple filamentation, and collision-induced absorption. The pressure optimum shifted to 10–15 atm for argon but to about 0.1 atm for CO2 owing to strong vibrational–rotational dissipation. The collection waveguide was strongly multimode; intermode interference and diffraction at its output produced the observed conical THz pattern and altered the inferred source parameters.
AI.conclusion: Molecular structure critically sets the pressure optimum for THz generation, and multimode waveguide collection can substantially transform the angular spectrum, so the conical far-field pattern does not directly represent the plasma-channel THz source.

title: CCGeant4: charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions in Geant4
summary: CCGeant4 models energy-loss fluctuations of heavy ions in Geant4, accounting for both charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation. We use GLOBAL cross sections for electron capture and loss, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers and charge-dependent delta-electron spectra calculated from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential. The package also supports tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering. The silicon example includes interference between Coulomb and nuclear scattering amplitudes. We compare charge evolution with GLOBAL and energy-loss spectra with MOCADI for matched beams and targets. Experimental comparisons cover the energy-loss measurements of Weick et al. and several measurements of energy deposited by xenon ions in silicon. For uranium at 800 MeV/u, the energy-loss variances from our Dirac configuration agree with the screened-ion calculations of Weick et al. to within 4% in Be, Al and Pb. Both calculations lie within the reported experimental uncertainties for all three targets, while calculated bismuth spectra in silver are narrower than measured. Calculations in thin silicon layers show that delta-electron escape can make deposited-energy distributions substantially narrower than primary-ion energy-loss distributions, highlighting the importance of secondary-electron transport for detector-response modelling. The distribution includes the Geant4 source patch, the transport tables and their converters, and a runnable example.

AI.tldr: CCGeant4 extends Geant4 to model charge-state-resolved transport and energy-loss fluctuations of relativistic heavy ions, including charge exchange, relativistic electron-scattering corrections, delta-electron spectra, and elastic ion-nucleus scattering, with validation against GLOBAL, MOCADI, and experimental data.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to improve heavy-ion energy-loss and detector-response modeling in Geant4 by accounting for charge exchange and relativistic corrections to electron scattering beyond the first Born approximation.
AI.method: CCGeant4 uses GLOBAL electron-capture and loss cross sections, ATIMA equilibrium stopping powers, charge-dependent delta-electron spectra from the Dirac equation in a frozen-shell potential, and optional tabulated elastic ion-nucleus scattering, including Coulomb-nuclear interference in a silicon example. Thin-silicon calculations show delta-electron escape can substantially narrow deposited-energy distributions relative to primary-ion energy-loss distributions.
AI.conclusion: Secondary-electron transport is important for detector-response modeling of relativistic heavy ions. The released package includes the Geant4 source patch, transport tables and converters, and a runnable example.

title: Flow Structure in Idealized Rotating Detonation Combustor with Supersonic Inflow
summary: The work presented investigates the flow structure and stability of an airbreathing rotating detonation engine (RDE) in an idealized combustor. The presented derivation of a modified pressure cutoff injection scheme allows for supersonic injection in an idealized two-dimensional RDE as a function of a specified design Mach number and the pressure ratio across the injection surface. Numerical simulations are conducted using a compressible reacting flow solver with finite-rate chemistry built on an Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) framework. The fuel mixture is set to a stoichiometric hydrogen-air mixture for all simulations. Stable operation occurs for a wide range of inflow conditions with inflow Mach numbers up to 4. The increased total temperature associated with increasing Mach numbers causes burning at the injection surface during the injector recovery process, resulting in unstable operation. Meanwhile, increasing total pressure facilitates sustained supersonic injection. Analysis of the steady flow structure shows a familiar structure with significant changes to the detonation structure when compared with a rocket RDE. With supersonic inflow, an oblique detonation wave (ODW) forms along the injection surface connected to the moving detonation through a slip line. Changes in the oblique detonation wave and normal detonation angle occur with changes in the inflow Mach number, however the overall detonation structure remains similar when supersonic injection occurs.

AI.tldr: An idealized two-dimensional airbreathing rotating detonation engine is simulated with a modified pressure-cutoff injection scheme; supersonic inflow up to Mach 4 can support stable operation, but higher total temperature can destabilize injection, and an oblique detonation wave forms along the injection surface.
AI.motivation: The work investigates the flow structure and stability of an airbreathing rotating detonation engine in an idealized combustor, particularly under supersonic injection conditions. The abstract does not provide broader application motivation beyond this investigation.
AI.method: The authors derive a modified pressure cutoff injection scheme that enables supersonic injection in an idealized two-dimensional RDE as a function of a specified design Mach number and the pressure ratio across the injection surface. Numerical simulations use a compressible reacting flow solver with finite-rate chemistry on an adaptive mesh refinement framework, with a stoichiometric hydrogen-air mixture in all simulations.
AI.result: Stable operation occurs over a wide range of inflow conditions with inflow Mach numbers up to 4. Increasing total temperature with Mach number causes burning at the injection surface during injector recovery, leading to unstable operation, while increasing total pressure facilitates sustained supersonic injection. The steady flow structure includes an oblique detonation wave along the injection surface connected to the moving detonation through a slip line; the oblique detonation wave and normal detonation angle change with inflow Mach number, but the overall detonation structure remains similar when supersonic injection occurs.
AI.conclusion: Supersonic injection can be sustained in the idealized RDE over a wide range of inflow conditions, but thermal effects associated with higher total temperature can cause injection-surface burning and instability. Increased total pressure supports sustained supersonic injection, and the resulting flow structure differs from that of a rocket RDE through the presence of an oblique detonation wave and slip line.

title: Phonon-mediated visible upconversion luminescence in femtosecond 1030-nm pumped Tm3+ -doped silica fibres
summary: We investigate multiphoton absorption-driven visible luminescence in a thulium-doped aluminosilicate optical fiber excited by an ultrafast 1030-nm femtosecond pulse train in the {MHz domain}. We report the observation of an unusual spectral crossover: the predominance of an emission band centered at 457-nm (deep blue) is progressively overtaken by a second emission, centered at 475-nm (cyan), as launched average power increases. Concurrently, a third near-infrared emission around 792~nm exhibits persistent, monotonic growth characterized by a well-defined bilinear slope transition. By combining calibrated spectral band integration with a structure-informed rate-equation model based on host thermodynamics, we show that the visible spectra evolution is governed by non-radiative multi-phonon transfer and phonon-assisted cross-relaxation activated by cumulative core heating, rather than permanent color-center solarization. These results offer new predictive insights into the thermal and spectroscopic stability of high-power ultrafast fiber systems.

AI.tldr: The paper studies visible upconversion luminescence in a Tm3+-doped aluminosilicate silica fiber pumped by an ultrafast 1030-nm femtosecond pulse train in the MHz domain, showing power-dependent spectral changes that are explained by heating-activated phonon processes rather than permanent color-center damage.
AI.motivation: The authors investigate multiphoton absorption-driven visible luminescence and its thermal/spectroscopic behavior in high-power ultrafast fiber systems; the abstract motivates this by the need for predictive insight into the thermal and spectroscopic stability of such systems.
AI.method: A thulium-doped aluminosilicate optical fiber is excited by an ultrafast 1030-nm femtosecond pulse train in the MHz domain. The authors combine calibrated spectral band integration with a structure-informed rate-equation model based on host thermodynamics to analyze the visible and near-infrared emission evolution.

title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
summary: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.

AI.tldr: Finite-N kinetic fluctuations in homogeneous long-range interacting systems without collective effects are shown to be captured exactly, at leading order in 1/N, by a closed deterministic hierarchy of three kinetic equations, avoiding large simulation ensembles.
AI.motivation: Finite-N fluctuations control the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, but obtaining their full statistics conventionally requires very large ensembles of computationally expensive simulations.
AI.method: Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, the authors derive the infinite hierarchy of n-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in 1/N and prove an exact quasi-Gaussian closure. This yields a minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy consisting of the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment; all higher-order moments follow algebraically.
AI.result: The hierarchy exactly preserves collisional invariants and their fluctuations and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against N-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance, and higher-order moments with accuracy that improves systematically with N.
AI.conclusion: A single deterministic time integration of three coupled partial differential equations replaces large ensembles of simulations for any large N in homogeneous systems without collective effects.

title: Analytic T-Matrix Formalism for Helmholtz Resonators
summary: We develop an analytic T-matrix formalism for two-dimensional circular acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls. The central idea is to use an aperture projection operator to obtain a compact expression for the T-matrix with explicit coefficients describing coupling and decoupling between external fields and cavity resonances. An equivalent formulation providing much faster convergence uses an aperture-to-Fourier map and an edge-adapted basis for the aperture flux. The method extends directly to multiple apertures of arbitrary angular widths and positions. The calculated scattering spectra agree with full-wave numerical simulations. For single- and double-aperture resonators, we decompose the T-matrix into even and odd parts under inversion to identify the channels associated with Willis coupling. We show how internal losses enable direction-dependent scattering and absorption when inversion symmetry is broken, while reciprocity ensures equal extinction for opposite incidence. Finally, we show how shifting the expansion origin redistributes radiation among multipole channels, enabling more compact T-matrix representations.

AI.tldr: The paper develops an analytic T-matrix formalism for two-dimensional circular acoustic Helmholtz resonators with thin rigid walls and multiple apertures, validates it against full-wave simulations, and uses it to analyze Willis coupling, loss-induced direction-dependent scattering and absorption, reciprocity, and multipole redistribution under origin shifts.
AI.motivation: The abstract does not explicitly state a broader motivation; its stated aim is to obtain a compact analytic T-matrix description of acoustic Helmholtz resonators with explicit coupling and decoupling between external fields and cavity resonances, including multiple apertures and channel analysis.
AI.method: An aperture projection operator yields a compact T-matrix with explicit coefficients for external-field/cavity-resonance coupling and decoupling. A faster-converging equivalent formulation uses an aperture-to-Fourier map and an edge-adapted basis for aperture flux. The approach extends to multiple apertures of arbitrary angular widths and positions; even/odd T-matrix decomposition under inversion and expansion-origin shifts are also used.

title: Thermal convection and jets produced by human exhalation dominate the indoor spreading of emitted CO$_2$ and aerosols
comment: 22 pages (main text 9 pages + Supplementary Information 13 pages), 14 figures, 4 tables
summary: For understanding airborne viral infection pathways, the prediction of the spreading and effective diffusivity of saliva droplets emitted from a person while speaking and breathing is crucial. In non-ventilated indoor spaces, the spreading of tracer particles or molecules emitted by a person is governed by the complex interplay of molecular diffusion, convection due to body heat and temperature boundary conditions as well as propulsion due to breathing in and out. By comparison of grid-based simulations of the compressible Navier-Stokes equation with experiments measuring the spreading of CO$_2$ emitted from a person, we demonstrate that molecular diffusion of CO$_2$ is present, but that the long-distance CO$_2$ spreading is completely dominated by the combination of convection due to body heat and temperature gradients at walls and windows and the periodic breathing pattern of a person. Breathing out induces long-range advection by a mid-Reynolds number flow pattern akin to the Landau-Squire jet, while breathing in creates only short-range flow. In conjunction with thermal convection, this symmetry breaking between breathing in and out produces fast long-distance transport of CO$_2$ and small aerosols.

AI.tldr: Grid-based compressible Navier-Stokes simulations compared with CO2 dispersion experiments show that indoor long-distance spreading of exhaled CO2 and small aerosols is dominated by thermal convection and periodic breathing jets rather than molecular diffusion.
AI.motivation: To understand airborne viral infection pathways by predicting the spreading and effective diffusivity of saliva droplets emitted during speaking and breathing in non-ventilated indoor spaces.
AI.method: The authors compared grid-based simulations of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with experiments measuring CO2 spreading from a person, accounting for molecular diffusion, convection from body heat and wall/window temperature gradients, and periodic inhalation/exhalation.
AI.result: Molecular diffusion of CO2 was present, but long-distance CO2 spreading was completely dominated by thermal convection combined with the periodic breathing pattern. Exhalation produced long-range advection via a mid-Reynolds-number flow akin to the Landau-Squire jet, whereas inhalation produced only short-range flow; this asymmetry, together with thermal convection, caused fast long-distance transport of CO2 and small aerosols.
AI.conclusion: Thermal convection and jets produced by human exhalation dominate the indoor long-distance spreading of emitted CO2 and small aerosols, with the inhalation-exhalation asymmetry enabling rapid transport in non-ventilated spaces.

title: PISim: A Unified Photonic Inference Simulator for Hardware-Aware Cross-Layer Design-Space Exploration
summary: Photonic neural accelerators offer ultra-low latency linear algebra, yet their usable numerical precision, sustainable throughput, and application accuracy remain tightly bounded by surrounding electro-optical interfaces and physical non-idealities. Pre-fabrication design-space exploration (DSE) requires a cross-layer electronic design automation (EDA) framework capable of evaluating disparate optical topologies under identical neural workloads and physical assumptions. We present \textbf{PISim}, a unified Photonic Inference Simulator that couples pretrained deep neural network execution with physics-based models of six accelerator architecture families, six electro-optic modulator technologies, four optical source organizations, and direct or coherent readout schemes. PISim embeds stage-resolved impairment operators---covering control and analog-to-digital quantization, finite extinction ratio, shot noise, correlated relative-intensity noise (RIN), thermal drift, propagation loss, and channel crosstalk---alongside an analytical cycle-level interface timing model to expose electronic-optical bottlenecks. Using simulated MNIST multilayer perceptron (MLP) benchmarks, we demonstrate how PISim identifies optimal precision operating points under multi-impairment stress (peaking at 6 bits for Mach--Zehnder and microring modulators), quantifies a 52.5 percentage-point accuracy gap between VCSEL-array and parallel-fanout laser architectures arising, under the modeled conditions, from power partitioning and correlated source noise, and models interface-limited throughput scaling across emitter-array widths from 32 to 128 channels. This comprehensive framework establishes an extensible, reproducible foundation for accuracy-constrained Pareto optimization prior to photonic tape-out.

title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
summary: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 πf(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

AI.tldr: One- and two-dimensional MHD-PIC simulations show that cosmic-ray electron acceleration in high-Mach-number, quasi-parallel supernova-remnant shocks becomes self-regulated: current-driven Bell turbulence limits the upstream cosmic-ray current and pressure precursor, while the downstream spectrum approaches test-particle diffusive shock acceleration.
AI.motivation: Efficient cosmic-ray acceleration should produce CR-modified shocks with smooth precursors and concave spectra, but observations favor spectra closer to the test-particle form or steeper. The paper investigates the long-term nonlinear coupling between thermal plasma and cosmic-ray electrons to clarify how injection and current-driven feedback affect shock structure and spectra.
AI.method: The authors perform one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations of non-relativistic, quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks, using electrons to probe current-driven feedback because of their larger charge-to-mass ratio. They vary the supplied cosmic-ray electron mass fraction and use a trajectory-based injection model that determines effective injection and acceleration through the evolving upstream turbulence rather than prescribing a shock injection fraction.
AI.result: The reflected cosmic-ray electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing a spatially extended cosmic-ray pressure precursor. Across the explored cosmic-ray electron mass supply, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream cosmic-ray current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle diffusive shock acceleration shape over the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure.
AI.conclusion: Once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state that is largely insensitive to the details of cosmic-ray injection.

title: Improving Nonequilibrium Thermal Conduction in CaF2 by Breaking the Phonon Bottleneck Effect
summary: Heat dissipation in laser optical materials depends not only on their thermal conductivity but also on how absorbed energy is redistributed among various phonon modes. In calcium fluoride (CaF2), rapid energy transfer from hot electrons to weakly propagating longitudinal optical (LO) phonons can create a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck effect that limits efficient heat removal. Here, we propose selective phonon excitation as an effective strategy to break this bottleneck. Combining electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we identify LO phonons as the primary modes that preferentially receive energy from hot carriers, leading to energy accumulation due to their inefficient transport and relaxation. Guided by three-phonon scattering phase-space analysis, selective excitation of transverse acoustic (TA) modes can accelerate LO relaxation and promote energy transfer toward heat-carrying acoustic modes. While sustained LO-phonon excitation reduces the thermal conductivity by approximately 12%, additional TA-mode excitation improves heat conduction by approximately 21% compared to the state limited by the LO-phonon bottleneck, surpassing the unexcited value. These findings demonstrate that controlling interbranch energy redistribution can counteract phonon-bottleneck-induced heat accumulation and reveal a working route for active thermal management in laser optical materials through selective control of phonon populations.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes selective phonon excitation to overcome a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck in CaF2, where hot-carrier energy accumulates in poorly transporting LO phonons. Using electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics, it shows that exciting TA modes accelerates LO relaxation and improves heat conduction beyond the bottleneck-limited state.
AI.motivation: Heat dissipation in laser optical materials depends on both thermal conductivity and how absorbed energy is redistributed among phonon modes. In CaF2, rapid transfer of energy from hot electrons to weakly propagating LO phonons creates a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck that hinders efficient heat removal, motivating strategies to break this bottleneck.
AI.method: The authors combine electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to identify the phonon modes receiving hot-carrier energy and the causes of energy accumulation. Guided by three-phonon scattering phase-space analysis, they examine selective excitation of TA modes as a way to accelerate LO-phonon relaxation and redirect energy toward heat-carrying acoustic modes.
AI.result: LO phonons are identified as the primary modes preferentially receiving energy from hot carriers, with energy accumulating because of inefficient transport and relaxation. Sustained LO-phonon excitation reduces thermal conductivity by approximately 12%, whereas additional TA-mode excitation improves heat conduction by approximately 21% relative to the LO-phonon-bottleneck-limited state, exceeding the unexcited value.
AI.conclusion: Controlling interbranch energy redistribution can counteract phonon-bottleneck-induced heat accumulation. Selective control of phonon populations provides a working route for active thermal management in laser optical materials.

title: Divergent Interfacial Lifetimes without Bulk Criticality in Fully Miscible Fluids
comment: 4 pages, 3 figures; Supplemental Material available as an ancillary file
summary: A fully miscible interface must disappear at equilibrium, but its lifetime need not be governed by a bulk instability. We construct a spatially resolved, dissipative two-field model in which a prepared correlation-excited interface undergoes a localized saddle-node while its homogeneous excited surroundings remain metastable and the relaxed mixture is strictly one phase. The interfacial soft mode produces a deterministic first-passage time that grows as the inverse square root of the distance from the fold and couples directly to the evolving concentration-profile width. The quartic structural potential admits an exact reduction from competing positive harmonic energies on a constrained configuration manifold; sixth- and eighth-order examples provide additional numerical robustness tests. The result is an interface-specific kinetic singularity without equilibrium bulk criticality, subject to explicitly stated microscopic and continuum limits.
