AI.conclusion: Next-generation ultrafast light sources are expected to provide decisive impact on understanding quantum and strongly correlated materials by addressing current capability gaps, but the abstract does not specify particular source requirements, experimental outcomes, or material systems.

title: Improving Airflow Network Models of Natural Ventilation: Geometry-Specific Pressures and Fluctuation Corrections
summary: Building energy models typically predict natural ventilation rates using airflow networks, which solve a system of orifice equations with exterior pressures as boundary conditions. This study investigates two improvements to these models: (i) geometry-specific exterior pressures obtained from large eddy simulations (LESs) and (ii) analytical corrections accounting for the nonlinear effects of pressure fluctuations on mean ventilation rates. We evaluate these improvements against coupled interior-exterior LESs of flows through 5824 windows, 2688 skylights, and 2752 interiors across idealized urban canopies. Replacing standard ASHRAE pressure coefficients with pressures from exterior-only LESs reduces the RMSE of predicted ventilation rates by approximately 50%, largely by capturing urban canopy flow effects that are poorly represented by standard shelter factors. Independently of the pressure source, mean-pressure airflow network predictions exhibit a nonlinear relationship with the LES ventilation rates. To address this discrepancy, we derive fluctuation corrections for mean-dominated and fluctuation-dominated flow regimes. These corrections eliminate the systematic nonlinearity and further reduce RMSE by 10-40% for most opening types and ventilation configurations. For windows, the combined improvements from geometry-specific surface pressures and fluctuation corrections increase the coefficient of determination $R^2$ from approximately 0.4 to 0.9. The results demonstrate the potential to accurately predict natural ventilation rates across different interior layouts while accounting for urban canopy effects and pressure fluctuations, using exterior-only LES pressure information.

AI.tldr: The paper improves airflow-network predictions of natural ventilation by using geometry-specific exterior pressures from large eddy simulations and analytical corrections for pressure-fluctuation nonlinearity, validated against coupled interior-exterior LES across idealized urban canopies.
AI.motivation: Standard building energy models predict natural ventilation with airflow networks using orifice equations and exterior pressure boundary conditions, but standard pressure coefficients and shelter factors may poorly represent urban canopy flow effects and pressure fluctuations. The study aims to improve ventilation-rate accuracy under these conditions.
AI.method: The authors evaluate two model improvements: geometry-specific exterior pressures obtained from exterior-only large eddy simulations (LESs), replacing standard ASHRAE pressure coefficients, and analytical fluctuation corrections for mean-dominated and fluctuation-dominated flow regimes. They benchmark predictions against coupled interior-exterior LESs for flows through 5824 windows, 2688 skylights, and 2752 interiors across idealized urban canopies.

title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
summary: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how organic spacer cations affect crystal symmetry and second-harmonic generation in quasi-2D halide perovskite single crystals, reporting strong, stable, anisotropic nonlinear optical emission linked to spacer-induced centrosymmetry breaking.
AI.motivation: Quasi-2D halide perovskites are tunable nonlinear optical platforms, but the relationship between organic spacer choice, crystal symmetry, and second-harmonic generation performance needs clarification to enable efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.
AI.method: The authors compare phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers in quasi-2D perovskite phases with varying numbers of [PbX6]4- layers. They fabricate high-quality crystals hundreds of micrometers wide using cavity-confined crystallization and characterize them with optical, power-dependent, and polarization-resolved second-harmonic generation measurements.

Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm its second-order nonlinear origin and reveal anisotropic emission patterns, establishing a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity.

title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
comment: 35 pages, 13 figures, 23 tables. Lead authors: Peter Sharpe and Carmelo Gonzales. Companion paper to "ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs" (Sharpe, 2026). Dataset to be published shortly at https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/AeroZoo
summary: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem in the form a solver receives it: the boundary meshes grouped by condition type, the prescribed values and the fluid properties. The 2,816 samples with a stable time mean form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, engineering metrics and 22 frozen splits, disjoint in geometry, that hold out geometry families, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of the inlet speed in single-seed runs (uniform inlet flow: 11.0%). ISLA, a transformer for boundary-driven PDEs, reaches 5.3% over four seeds, about 4 times the change from a finer mesh. On the same test samples, a held-out geometry family barely changes ISLA's error relative to uniform flow, and a held-out enclosure or boundary-condition layout raises it 2.4 to 9.2 times. title: Subpicosecond Optical Time Transfer under Simulated Motion with Electro-Optic Frequency Combs
summary: Extension of high performance optical frequency comb-based time transfer to real-world systems is challenged by platform motion, particularly for large relative velocities. Here, we utilize agile electro-optic frequency combs to construct a laboratory-based simulator of a two-way optical time transfer system under motion. Through direct control of the electro-optic frequency comb parameters, we can artificially induce the effects of relative motion. We performed tests of the time transfer performance across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles that linearly increase from rest up to 400 m/s. Through a post-processed data analysis, we demonstrate continuous tracking of the clock offset between sites with subpicosecond precision throughout the velocity sweep. These results illustrate the versatility of using electro-optic frequency combs for optical time transfer in deployed systems.

AI.tldr: The paper uses agile electro-optic frequency combs to simulate a two-way optical time-transfer system under relative motion over a km-scale fiber link, demonstrating continuous clock-offset tracking with subpicosecond precision during velocity sweeps up to 400 m/s.
AI.motivation: Extending high-performance optical frequency comb-based time transfer to real-world systems is challenged by platform motion, especially large relative velocities.

Direct control of the comb parameters artificially induced relative-motion effects, and time-transfer performance was tested across a km-scale fiber link for velocity profiles increasing linearly from rest to 400 m/s, followed by post-processed data analysis.

title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
comment: 48 pages, 14 figures, 26 tables. Companion paper to "AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics" (Sharpe et al., 2026)
summary: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.

AI.tldr: ISLA is a coordinate-free, measure-weighted slice-attention transformer for steady boundary-driven PDEs. It removes coordinates from learned operations, treats boundary sums as quadrature, and uses boundary-relative distances, angles, and units. It is rigid-motion/reflection equivariant, unit invariant, and mesh-refinement consistent. It substantially outperforms baselines on AeroZoo and ranks second only to GLOBE on AirfRANS.

The paper argues that surrogate models should respect coordinate-frame, unit, and mesh invariance.

No learned operation receives a coordinate; positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors; lengths use a unit computed from the boundary; every boundary sum is a quadrature; each boundary cell is a token with an exact boundary read; and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another.

On AeroZoo, across 2,816 flows varying in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline. On AirfRANS, its errors are second only to the boundary-integral model GLOBE and at least 1.6 times lower than Transolver and GeoTransolver.
AI.conclusion: The proposed coordinate-free, measure-weighted transformer provides a more invariant and accurate surrogate for boundary-driven PDEs, with strong gains on AeroZoo and competitive performance on AirfRANS. The abstract does not provide details on computational cost, training data requirements, or performance beyond these benchmarks.

title: Metasurfaces with Anisotropic Electric and Magnetic Conductivities: Parameter Retrieval for Arbitrary Incidence and Polarization
summary: Metasurfaces come in a great variety of unit cell geometries and material composition. A common approach for describing them relies on retrieving effective surface parameters (e.g., electric and magnetic conductivities) from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells, a uniform host material, or lead to increased complexity by requiring reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface. Here, we derive analytical expressions for the equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically- and magnetically-polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The proposed formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information, thus simplifying the process especially in experimental studies. The method is validated through representative electric and magnetic meta-atoms at microwave and THz frequencies, respectively. Their ability for polarization conversion is demonstrated and discussed relying on the physical insight provided by the retrieved anisotropic conductivities. In addition, we present the inverse expressions for calculating the reflection and transmission coefficients from known surface conductivity tensors, which can prove useful for metasurface synthesis and radiation problems.

AI.tldr: The paper derives analytical retrieval expressions for anisotropic electric and magnetic surface conductivities of metasurfaces under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization, avoiding bidirectional scattering data, validating the method with microwave and THz meta-atoms, and providing inverse expressions for reflection and transmission.
AI.motivation: Metasurfaces have diverse geometries and compositions, and effective surface parameters are commonly retrieved from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells or a uniform host material, or become more complex because they require reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface.
AI.method: The authors derive analytical expressions for equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically and magnetically polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information. The method is validated using representative electric and magnetic meta-atoms at microwave and THz frequencies, respectively. Inverse expressions are also presented for calculating reflection and transmission coefficients from known surface conductivity tensors.
AI.result: The proposed retrieval method is validated with representative electric and magnetic meta-atoms at microwave and THz frequencies. Their polarization-conversion capability is demonstrated and discussed using physical insight from the retrieved anisotropic conductivities. Inverse expressions for reflection and transmission from known conductivity tensors are also provided. No quantitative accuracy or bandwidth metrics are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: The formulation simplifies retrieval of anisotropic surface conductivities by avoiding bidirectional scattering information, which is especially advantageous for experimental studies. The inverse expressions may be useful for metasurface synthesis and radiation problems.

title: Sedimentation of flexible fibers through an ordered array of pillars
summary: In this study, we extend our previous work [Makanga \textit{et al.}, Physical Review Fluids 8, 044303 (2023)] to investigate the effects of a periodic array of pillars on the settling dynamics of a flexible fiber in a viscous fluid. By means of numerical simulations, we show that the fiber trajectory falls at long times into one of two migration modes, ``zigzag" and ``displacement", which are determined by the short-time scattering dynamics induced by fiber-pillar interactions. In the zigzag mode, there is no average displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the center of mass of the fiber follows a quasi-straight line. Conversely, in the displacement mode, there is a net displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the fiber center of mass follows a cyclical skew-bumping path. We show how this long-time behavior can be predicted using a theoretical model with minimal ingredients. These findings, together with the long-time transport properties of the fiber, provide insights into future experiments, as well as the design of gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement (DLD) devices to sort elongated particles based on their geometric and/or mechanical properties.

AI.tldr: Numerical simulations show that a flexible fiber settling in a viscous fluid through a periodic pillar array adopts either a zigzag mode with no net displacement along gravity or a displacement mode with net displacement and a cyclical skew-bumping path; the long-time mode is set by short-time fiber-pillar scattering and can be predicted by a minimal theoretical model.
AI.motivation: The study extends previous work to determine how a periodic array of pillars affects the settling dynamics of a flexible fiber in a viscous fluid, with implications for experiments and for designing gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement devices that sort elongated particles by geometric and/or mechanical properties.
AI.method: The authors use numerical simulations of a flexible fiber sedimenting through an ordered periodic pillar array in a viscous fluid and develop a theoretical model with minimal ingredients to predict the long-time migration behavior from short-time fiber-pillar interactions.
AI.result: At long times the fiber follows one of two migration modes, zigzag or displacement, determined by short-time scattering dynamics induced by fiber-pillar interactions. In the zigzag mode there is no average displacement relative to gravity and the center of mass follows a quasi-straight line; in the displacement mode there is a net displacement relative to gravity and the center of mass follows a cyclical skew-bumping path.
AI.conclusion: The long-time behavior can be predicted using a minimal theoretical model. These findings and the fiber's long-time transport properties provide insights for future experiments and for the design of gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement devices to sort elongated particles by geometric and/or mechanical properties.

title: Towards dense optical communications with partially coherent light: II. Multimode Stokes communications
summary: Partially coherent light has a higher informational-carrying capacity than coherent light when both fields are spanned by the same modes, which implies that partially coherent light may increase the channel density in optical communications. A partially coherent field spanned by $N_{\mathrm{f}}$ modes can multiplex $N_{\mathrm{D}}=N_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-1$ data streams in the generalized Stokes parameters that uniquely identify its coherence matrix -- a scheme we call `Stokes communications' (S-Comm). We have proposed in an accompanying paper a realization of S-Comm for bimodal fields $N_{\mathrm{f}}=2$ that multiplex $N_{\mathrm{D}}=3$ data streams. Here we extend this proposed strategy for S-Comm to multimode fields $N_{\mathrm{f}}>2$. We find that the diagonal and off-diagonal Stokes parameters require different treatments and we provide detailed designs for the transmitter and receiver for both diagonally and off-diagonally multiplexed data streams. The building blocks of the proposed system can be readily implemented in integrated photonic circuit platforms. Our results indicate that on-chip processing of multimode partially coherent light (or `structured coherence') may have profound implications for optical communications and for optical signal processing in general.

AI.tldr: The paper extends Stokes communications (S-Comm) from bimodal to multimode partially coherent fields, showing that Nf modes can multiplex Nf^2−1 data streams in generalized Stokes parameters and presenting transmitter/receiver designs suitable for integrated photonic circuits.
AI.motivation: Partially coherent light can carry more information than coherent light when both are spanned by the same modes, suggesting it may increase channel density in optical communications.
AI.method: The authors generalize S-Comm, which encodes data in the generalized Stokes parameters of the coherence matrix, to multimode fields with Nf>2. They treat diagonal and off-diagonal Stokes parameters separately and provide detailed transmitter and receiver designs for diagonally and off-diagonally multiplexed data streams.
AI.result: The paper provides multimode S-Comm designs for both diagonal and off-diagonal multiplexing and states that the system's building blocks can be readily implemented in integrated photonic circuit platforms. No quantitative performance results are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: On-chip processing of multimode partially coherent light, or structured coherence, may have profound implications for optical communications and optical signal processing more generally.

title: Complex nematic dynamics driven by steady Kolmogorov flows
summary: Complex nematohydrodynamics, including irregular defect dynamics, is commonly associated with time-dependent flows, most notably in active turbulence. Here we consider a simple model of a planar nematic subjected to a temporally steady but spatially varying flow and investigate the onset of time-dependent dynamics. Subjecting a passive nematic to steady Kolmogorov flow, while eliminating velocity fluctuations and hydrodynamic feedback, we find that increasing the flow strength drives a transition from stationary to periodic and, at stronger forcing, irregular spatiotemporal dynamics. The time-dependent states involve repeated local suppression of nematic order and director reorganisation, arising from the competition between spatially varying shear and nematic relaxation. Bifurcation and phase-space analyses characterise this progression, while reduced-order models identify the dynamical origins. A two-mode model captures the onset of periodic motion through a saddle-node infinite-period bifurcation. A five-mode Galerkin truncation further recovers the progression from stationary to periodic and irregular dynamics. These results allow us to explain how a fixed, spatially heterogeneous velocity field can generate temporal complexity through the nonlinear dynamics of nematic order alone.

AI.tldr: A passive planar nematic under a steady, spatially varying Kolmogorov flow transitions from stationary to periodic and then irregular spatiotemporal dynamics as flow strength increases, with reduced-order models explaining the bifurcations and dynamical origins.
AI.motivation: Complex nematohydrodynamics and irregular defect dynamics are usually linked to time-dependent flows such as active turbulence; this work asks whether a temporally steady but spatially heterogeneous velocity field can alone generate temporal complexity in nematic order.
AI.method: The authors study a simple planar nematic model subjected to steady Kolmogorov flow while eliminating velocity fluctuations and hydrodynamic feedback. They vary flow strength, perform bifurcation and phase-space analyses, and use reduced-order models: a two-mode model and a five-mode Galerkin truncation.
AI.result: Increasing flow strength drives a transition from stationary to periodic dynamics and, at stronger forcing, to irregular spatiotemporal dynamics. The time-dependent states involve repeated local suppression of nematic order and director reorganisation due to competition between spatially varying shear and nematic relaxation. A two-mode model captures the onset of periodic motion via a saddle-node infinite-period bifurcation, and a five-mode Galerkin truncation recovers the progression from stationary to periodic and irregular dynamics. Quantitative parameter values and specific irregularity measures are not provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: A fixed, spatially heterogeneous velocity field can generate temporal complexity through the nonlinear dynamics of nematic order alone, without time-dependent forcing or hydrodynamic feedback.

title: Towards dense optical communications with partially coherent light: I. Bimodal Stokes communications
summary: In conventional optical multiplexing, $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~orthogonal spectral or spatial modes multiplex $N_{\mathrm{f}}$ independent data streams transmitted over an optical channel (e.g., a multimode optical fiber supporting $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~guided modes). We introduce here a new optical communications scheme that we call `Stokes communications' (S-Comm), whereby $N_{\mathrm{D}}=N_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-1$ independent data streams are multiplexed into $N_{\mathrm{f}}$~optical modes, potentially yielding a dramatic increase in the channel capacity. Rather than modulating the amplitude of each mode to encode a data stream, we make use of multimode partially coherent light and modulate each generalized Stokes parameter in the $N_{\mathrm{f}}\times N_{\mathrm{f}}$ Hermitian coherence matrix associated with the field. We present here designs for the S-Comm transmitter and receiver making use of bimodal fields ($N_{\mathrm{f}}=2$) in which $N_{\mathrm{D}}=3$ data streams are encoded via on-off keying and multiplexed in two modes. We describe the main blocks in the S-Comm transmitter: coherence modulators that encode a data stream in the degree of coherence of a bimode (a two-mode partially coherent field), Stokes encoders that assign each data stream to a prescribed Stokes parameter, and Stokes multiplexers that combine bimodes into physical modes. We also describe the reverse operations implemented in the S-Comm receiver to recover the data streams. Significantly higher channel capacity is expected for a larger number of physical modes, which is facilitated by the amenability of the presented designs to on-chip integration. These results suggest that the long-appreciated but unexploited higher information-carrying capacity of partially coherent light can help realize dense optical communications.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Stokes communications (S-Comm), an optical multiplexing scheme that encodes up to N_D=N_f^2−1 independent data streams in N_f optical modes by modulating generalized Stokes parameters of the multimode coherence matrix, and presents bimodal transmitter/receiver designs for three on-off-keyed data streams in two modes.
AI.motivation: Conventional optical multiplexing uses N_f orthogonal spectral or spatial modes to carry only N_f independent data streams, leaving the higher information-carrying capacity of partially coherent light largely unexploited. The authors aim to realize denser optical communications by exploiting this capacity.
AI.method: S-Comm uses multimode partially coherent light and modulates each generalized Stokes parameter in the N_f×N_f Hermitian coherence matrix rather than modulating each mode amplitude. For bimodal fields with N_f=2, the paper presents transmitter designs containing coherence modulators that encode data in the degree of coherence of a bimode, Stokes encoders that assign data streams to prescribed Stokes parameters, and Stokes multiplexers that combine bimodes into physical modes, plus receiver designs implementing the reverse operations; three data streams are encoded via on-off keying and multiplexed in two modes.
AI.result: The proposed bimodal S-Comm designs multiplex N_D=3 independent data streams into N_f=2 optical modes using on-off keying, with transmitter and receiver block designs described. The authors state that significantly higher channel capacity is expected for a larger number of physical modes, facilitated by the designs' amenability to on-chip integration.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that the long-appreciated but previously unexploited higher information-carrying capacity of partially coherent light can help realize dense optical communications.

title: Elasto-inertial force exerted on a sphere oscillating in a fluid near a soft interface
summary: Fluid inertia can remain important in confined flows, even at low Reynolds number when convective inertia is negligible; yet its coupling with interface deformability is an open problem. Here, we theoretically investigate the high-frequency oscillations of an immersed sphere near an elastic wall in the lubrication regime. We first reconcile previous predictions for the added mass near a rigid wall by consistently matching the inner lubrication flow with the outer flow. Using this rigid-wall problem as a reference, we then develop a perturbative analysis of wall deformation and derive the leading elasto-inertial correction to the hydrodynamic force. Our results reveal that the coupling between interface softness and fluid inertia produces a dominant non-dissipative force contribution scaling as the power four of the frequency in the high-frequency limit, thus corresponding to the fourth time derivative of the sphere's position. This finding may have implications regarding the short-time dynamics of colloidal particles near deformable interfaces in biological and soft-matter settings.

AI.tldr: This theoretical study analyzes high-frequency oscillations of a sphere in a viscous fluid near an elastic wall in the lubrication regime. By matching inner lubrication and outer flows for the rigid-wall reference and then perturbatively incorporating wall deformation, it derives the leading elasto-inertial hydrodynamic force, which includes a dominant non-dissipative term proportional to frequency to the fourth power.
AI.motivation: Fluid inertia can remain important in confined low-Reynolds-number flows, but its coupling with interface deformability is an open problem. The paper aims to understand how softness of a nearby elastic wall modifies inertial hydrodynamic forces on an oscillating sphere.
AI.method: The authors perform a theoretical lubrication-regime analysis of a sphere oscillating at high frequency near an elastic wall. They first reconcile previous added-mass predictions for a rigid wall by consistently matching the inner lubrication flow with the outer flow, then use the rigid-wall solution as a reference for a perturbative analysis of wall deformation and derive the leading elasto-inertial correction to the hydrodynamic force.
AI.result: The coupling between interface softness and fluid inertia produces a dominant non-dissipative force contribution that scales as the fourth power of frequency in the high-frequency limit, corresponding to the fourth time derivative of the sphere's position.
AI.conclusion: The derived elasto-inertial force may have implications for the short-time dynamics of colloidal particles near deformable interfaces in biological and soft-matter settings.

title: Gradient-Free Inverse Design of 3D Nanophotonic Devices Using the Level-Set-Method
summary: Advances in 3D nanophotonic additive manufacturing enable increasingly complex, almost free-form devices for manipulating light at sub-wavelength scales. Extending nanophotonic designs into three dimensions introduces additional degrees of freedom. Exploiting this freedom requires inverse-design methods that can efficiently navigate this large design space while accommodating fabrication constraints. Here, we combine gradient-free optimization with the level-set method (LSM) to provide such an approach for 3D additive manufacturing. Representing the 3D geometry as a level set constructed from Gaussian radial basis functions retains substantial geometric freedom with only a few hundred design variables. This compact representation makes gradient-free optimization practical for fully 3D nanophotonic devices, eliminating the need for adjoint calculations. This unlocks the use of any Maxwell solver or auxiliary algorithms that should express fabrication constraints for which the required derivatives are unavailable or impractical to obtain, and enables embarrassingly parallel workflows. Consequently, binary fabrication requirements, such as structural connectivity, can be rigorously enforced, avoiding the differentiable approximations commonly used in gradient-based optimization. Here, we demonstrate the combination of the gradient-free LSM with a connected-component analysis algorithm to enforce the structural integrity of the design. We demonstrate the applicability of the gradient-free LSM by optimizing a Y-splitter while strictly enforcing the structural integrity of the material and the void in the design.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a gradient-free level-set inverse-design method for fully 3D nanophotonic devices fabricated by additive manufacturing. It uses a compact Gaussian-radial-basis-function level-set representation to reduce the design space, avoids adjoint derivatives, and enforces binary fabrication constraints such as structural connectivity, demonstrated by optimizing a Y-splitter with strict material and void integrity.
AI.motivation: 3D nanophotonic additive manufacturing enables complex, nearly free-form devices for sub-wavelength light manipulation, and moving designs into three dimensions adds design degrees of freedom. Exploiting these degrees of freedom requires inverse-design methods that can efficiently explore a large design space while accommodating fabrication constraints.
AI.method: The authors combine gradient-free optimization with the level-set method (LSM). The 3D geometry is represented as a level set constructed from Gaussian radial basis functions, retaining substantial geometric freedom with only a few hundred design variables. This compact representation makes gradient-free optimization practical for fully 3D nanophotonic devices and eliminates the need for adjoint calculations. It also allows use of any Maxwell solver or auxiliary fabrication-constraint algorithms whose derivatives are unavailable or impractical, and supports embarrassingly parallel workflows. A connected-component analysis algorithm is combined with the gradient-free LSM to enforce structural integrity, including binary fabrication requirements.
AI.result: The approach is demonstrated by optimizing a Y-splitter while strictly enforcing the structural integrity of both the material and the void in the design. The abstract does not provide quantitative performance metrics for the optimized device.
AI.conclusion: Gradient-free LSM is a practical inverse-design approach for fully 3D nanophotonic devices because its compact level-set representation reduces the number of design variables, avoids adjoint calculations, enables use of arbitrary Maxwell solvers and fabrication-constraint algorithms, and permits rigorous enforcement of binary fabrication requirements such as structural connectivity.

title: Stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links hold echinocytes in a model splenic slit
comment: 35 pages, 8 figures, 1 table; Supplementary Materials included (pages S1-S16, 6 figures, 1 table); Movies S1 to S3 are ancillary files. The first two authors contributed equally
summary: Stored red blood cells become echinocytes, growing spicules before losing membrane; the spleen clears the resulting small, spherical cells. Whether spicules alone hinder splenic passage is unknown. Shape and area change together. In a two-component model whose shrinking cytoskeleton raises spicules, we drove a discocyte and stage I to III echinocytes of equal area and volume through a model splenic slit. The pressure drop needed to pass rose with stage; stage III echinocytes were held at 37 to 50 times the pressure drop that passed the discocyte. Bilayer-cytoskeleton links stretched near full extension held these cells; lengthening them about twofold released a held cell. Capillary-sized channels, as in our device, separated the stages far less. Of the shape classes in stored blood, the model held at high pressure drops only storage-induced microerythrocytes, which perfused human spleens clear most. Spicules, besides membrane loss, may decide which stored cells the spleen retains.

AI.tldr: A two-component model shows that stage I–III echinocytes of equal area and volume require progressively higher pressure drops to traverse a model splenic slit, with stage III cells held at 37–50 times the discocyte pressure drop by stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links.
AI.motivation: Stored red blood cells become echinocytes with spicules before membrane loss, and the spleen clears small spherical cells, but whether spicules alone hinder splenic passage was unknown; shape and area change together, motivating controlled comparison at equal area and volume.
AI.method: The authors used a two-component model in which a shrinking cytoskeleton raises spicules and drove discocytes and stage I to III echinocytes of equal area and volume through a model splenic slit, measuring the pressure drop required for passage and testing release by lengthening bilayer-cytoskeleton links.
AI.result: The pressure drop needed to pass increased with echinocyte stage; stage III echinocytes were held at 37 to 50 times the pressure drop that passed the discocyte. Bilayer-cytoskeleton links stretched near full extension held these cells, and lengthening them about twofold released a held cell. Capillary-sized channels separated the stages far less. Among shape classes in stored blood, only storage-induced microerythrocytes were held at high pressure drops, and perfused human spleens clear most of these.
AI.conclusion: Spicules, in addition to membrane loss, may determine which stored red blood cells the spleen retains, because stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links can hold echinocytes in a model splenic slit at high pressure drops.

title: Laser-induced damage threshold of periodic plasmonic metasurfaces
summary: Plasmonic metasurfaces enable strong nonlinear optical responses due to sub-wavelength field confinement, yet their performance is fundamentally limited by low laser-induced damage thresholds (LIDT). Here, we present a comprehensive experimental and numerical study of the interplay between surface lattice resonances (SLRs), second-harmonic generation (SHG), and LIDT in periodic gold nanobar metasurfaces. Angle-resolved measurements reveal that excitation of SLRs at the fundamental wavelength strongly enhances SHG efficiency while simultaneously reducing the LIDT. In contrast, excitation of an SLR at the second-harmonic wavelength does not affect the damage threshold, allowing the SHG signal to be maximized. Our findings establish a fundamental trade-off between nonlinear efficiency and optical robustness and provide design guidelines for optimizing periodic plasmonic metasurfaces for high-power nonlinear applications.

AI.tldr: This study experimentally and numerically examines periodic gold nanobar plasmonic metasurfaces, showing that surface lattice resonance excitation at the fundamental wavelength enhances second-harmonic generation but lowers the laser-induced damage threshold, while excitation at the second-harmonic wavelength preserves the damage threshold and enables higher SHG.
AI.motivation: Plasmonic metasurfaces provide strong nonlinear optical responses through sub-wavelength field confinement, but their practical performance is limited by low laser-induced damage thresholds. The paper aims to clarify the interplay among surface lattice resonances, second-harmonic generation, and laser-induced damage threshold.
AI.method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental and numerical study of periodic gold nanobar metasurfaces using angle-resolved measurements. They compare excitation of surface lattice resonances at the fundamental wavelength and at the second-harmonic wavelength with respect to SHG efficiency and damage threshold.
AI.result: Excitation of a surface lattice resonance at the fundamental wavelength strongly enhances SHG efficiency while simultaneously reducing the laser-induced damage threshold. In contrast, excitation of a surface lattice resonance at the second-harmonic wavelength does not affect the damage threshold, allowing the SHG signal to be maximized.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish a fundamental trade-off between nonlinear efficiency and optical robustness in periodic plasmonic metasurfaces and provide design guidelines for optimizing such metasurfaces for high-power nonlinear applications.

title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
summary: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

AI.tldr: Laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs under confinement generate high-speed microjets whose localized shear enhances crystal nucleation; microjet velocity correlates with crystallization probability, and shear is incorporated into classical nucleation theory.
AI.motivation: Primary nucleation controls the physicochemical, optical, and mechanical properties of solution-grown crystals, but a nucleation mechanism driven by bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions had not been recognized. The paper aims to identify and quantify microjet-induced crystallization.
AI.method: The study used laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs under confinement to generate antiphase bubbles and a micron-scale high-speed liquid jet in supersaturated potassium permanganate solution. It compared paired-bubble experiments with single-bubble controls under identical laser energies and supersaturation, varied microjet velocity, performed boundary integral simulations of confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy effects, and incorporated shear into the kinetic prefactor of classical nucleation theory.
AI.result: Microjet impact produced intense localized shear and induced crystallization of potassium permanganate, whereas crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments without a microjet under identical conditions. Crystallization probability increased with microjet velocity. Simulations showed how confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity, and the shear-modified kinetic prefactor quantified the enhancement in nucleation kinetics.
AI.conclusion: Microjets generated by hydrodynamic interactions between thermocavitation bubbles can influence crystallization kinetics, establishing a bubble-bubble interaction mechanism for nucleation and suggesting opportunities for crystalline materials manufacturing.

title: Ultrahigh-speed digital holography reveals blood flow beneath the skin
summary: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) leverages ultrahigh-speed digital holography to reveal blood-flow signals in vessels beneath the skin of the closed eyelid and around the eye. We demonstrate this in one volunteer using recordings acquired at approximately 16,000 frames/s under 10~mW of diffuse near-infrared illumination. Numerical Fresnel reconstruction and principal-component filtering reveal branching vascular patterns. These results extend an ocular imaging system to blood-flow visualization beneath the skin without requiring elaborate immobilization procedures.

AI.tldr: Laser Doppler holography recorded at about 16,000 frames/s under 10 mW diffuse near-infrared illumination was used in one volunteer to visualize blood-flow signals and branching vascular patterns beneath the skin of the closed eyelid and around the eye, extending an ocular imaging system without elaborate immobilization.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to extend an ocular imaging system to blood-flow visualization beneath the skin, including beneath the closed eyelid and around the eye, without requiring elaborate immobilization procedures.
AI.method: The authors used laser Doppler holography with ultrahigh-speed digital holography, acquiring recordings at approximately 16,000 frames/s under 10 mW of diffuse near-infrared illumination in one volunteer. Numerical Fresnel reconstruction and principal-component filtering were used to reveal vascular patterns.
AI.result: The method revealed blood-flow signals in vessels beneath the skin of the closed eyelid and around the eye, with numerical reconstruction and filtering showing branching vascular patterns.
AI.conclusion: Ultrahigh-speed laser Doppler holography can visualize blood flow beneath the skin and extends an ocular imaging system to this application without elaborate immobilization; the demonstration involved one volunteer.

title: Soft material mechanical property degradation at high strain rates
summary: The rheometry of soft, tissue-like materials at ultra-high strain rates is critical to biomechanics, materials science, and medical engineering. One approach for characterizing high-rate material response is Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry (IMR), which infers viscoelastic constitutive behavior from the measured radius-time history of a laser-induced cavitation bubble. At these rates, materials may exhibit history-dependent behavior, including damage, fracture, and plasticity. However, conventional IMR analyses typically assume constant material properties throughout the cavitation event, limiting their ability to capture such changes. We present an IMR framework for identifying effective time varying material properties from measured cavitation radius histories. The framework allows the shear modulus, viscosity, or both to evolve during the event using normalized sigmoid histories. Synthetic tests recover prescribed constant and time varying material histories. Application to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets yields effective material-property histories across formulations and experimental conditions. Viscosity decreased across the datasets, while the extent of shear modulus reduction varied with material and formulation. When both properties decreased, their reductions could occur at different stages of cavitation. This distinction in mechanical property degradation depends on both the property and its evolution during high-strain events.

AI.tldr: A new Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry framework infers time-varying shear modulus and viscosity of soft materials from laser-induced cavitation radius histories, capturing property degradation at high strain rates.
AI.motivation: Soft, tissue-like materials can exhibit history-dependent damage, fracture, and plasticity at ultra-high strain rates, but conventional Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry assumes constant material properties during cavitation and therefore cannot capture such changes.
AI.method: The authors develop an Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry framework that identifies effective time-varying material properties from measured cavitation radius-time histories, allowing shear modulus, viscosity, or both to evolve via normalized sigmoid histories. They validate it with synthetic tests and apply it to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets.
AI.result: Synthetic tests recover prescribed constant and time-varying material histories. In polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets, viscosity decreased across formulations and experimental conditions, while the extent of shear modulus reduction varied with material and formulation; when both properties decreased, their reductions could occur at different stages of cavitation.
AI.conclusion: The framework can identify effective time-varying mechanical properties during high-strain-rate cavitation and reveals that mechanical property degradation depends on both the property and its evolution during the event.

title: A Field-Deployable 2U Ultra-Stable Laser with Sub-Hertz Linewidth Based on Optoelectronic Oscillator Locking
summary: Compact, high-performance ultra-stable lasers that can operate outside the laboratory remain a long-standing goal. Here we report, to our knowledge, the most compact field-deployable ultra-stable laser, packaged in a standard 2U rack chassis. It is stabilized to a 50 mm-long, 19 mL optical reference cavity with low vibration sensitivity by optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) locking, an approach particularly suited to compact, transportable systems. The laser delivers an integrated linewidth of about 0.42 Hz and a fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s averaging time (about 2.2E-15 at 0.4 s). Measured phase noise approaches the cavity thermal-noise limit below 100 Hz and the theoretical OEO-locking limit from 100 Hz to 100 kHz. The system volume is roughly one quarter of the volume of previously reported integrated, transportable ultra-stable lasers of comparable performance, making it well suited for field applications in time-frequency metrology, quantum technologies, and environmental sensing.

AI.tldr: The paper reports a field-deployable 2U rack-mounted ultra-stable laser stabilized by optoelectronic oscillator locking to a compact 50 mm-long, 19 mL low-vibration-sensitivity optical reference cavity. It achieves approximately 0.42 Hz integrated linewidth and fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s, with a system volume about one quarter that of previously reported integrated transportable ultra-stable lasers of comparable performance.
AI.motivation: Compact, high-performance ultra-stable lasers that can operate outside the laboratory are a long-standing goal; existing integrated transportable systems of comparable performance are relatively large, motivating a more compact field-deployable design.
AI.method: The laser is packaged in a standard 2U rack chassis and stabilized to a 50 mm-long, 19 mL optical reference cavity with low vibration sensitivity using optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) locking, which the authors describe as particularly suited to compact, transportable systems.
AI.result: The system delivers an integrated linewidth of about 0.42 Hz and fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s averaging time (about 2.2E-15 at 0.4 s). Measured phase noise approaches the cavity thermal-noise limit below 100 Hz and the theoretical OEO-locking limit from 100 Hz to 100 kHz. Its volume is roughly one quarter that of previously reported integrated, transportable ultra-stable lasers with comparable performance.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that this is, to their knowledge, the most compact field-deployable ultra-stable laser and that it is well suited for field applications in time-frequency metrology, quantum technologies, and environmental sensing.

title: Fragility of Aeolian Ripples
summary: Sand surfaces exposed to the wind are covered by aeolian sand waves of diverse wavelengths, from centimetres for small ripples to decameters for dunes. Sand dunes can be said to be antifragile, since their growth is not prohibited by storms, whereas ripples and megaripples are fragile since they get flattened. The fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes their fragility to a common cause: the spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains. Here, we challenge this conventional view by revealing its major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative framework, routed in the granular bed rheology, posits that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface gives way to a three-phase flow, featuring an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Notably, both martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which emerge via a hydrodynamic instability, are insensitive to such "surface-melting". Their destruction is predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, instead. Our theoretical arguments are well supported by a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter, assembled from a carefully reassessed large body of literature, and backed up by dedicated control measurements.

AI.tldr: The paper challenges the conventional fluid-entrainment explanation for the fragility of aeolian ripples and proposes a granular-bed-rheology framework in which impact ripples are erased by a transition from two-phase ballistic grain hopping to a three-phase, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. It distinguishes this behavior from that of martian wind-drag and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, whose destruction is instead linked to a transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, and supports the arguments with a reassessed literature-derived stability diagram and dedicated control measurements.
AI.motivation: The conventional fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes the fragility of ripples and megaripples to spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains, but the paper argues that this view has major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative explanation is needed for why ripples and megaripples are flattened while dunes can grow despite storms.
AI.method: The authors critically reassess the fluid-entrainment hypothesis and develop an alternative theoretical framework based on granular bed rheology. They assemble a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter from a carefully reassessed large body of literature and back up their theoretical arguments with dedicated control measurements. Specific experimental protocols and measurement details are not provided in the abstract.
AI.result: The paper reports inconsistencies in the conventional fluid-entrainment view. It proposes that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface transitions to a three-phase flow containing an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which arise via a hydrodynamic instability, are described as insensitive to this surface-melting process; their destruction is instead predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions. The stability diagram and control measurements are said to support these arguments.
AI.conclusion: The fragility of aeolian ripples is not adequately explained by spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment alone. A granular-bed-rheology framework, together with the aerodynamic smooth-to-rough transition for wind-drag and aerodynamic ripples, provides a more consistent explanation that is supported by a reassessed literature-derived stability diagram and dedicated control measurements.

title: High-directivity pulsed beams for effective power and information transfer
summary: A vector spherical wave expansion (VSWE) is used to engineer an elemental multipole source whose radiated field is a superdirective, extremely unidirectional (SDEU) needle beam. It is proved analytically and confirmed numerically that the element attains Harrington's normal-directivity value along its beam axis. Its radiated field is linearly polarized with an azimuthally symmetric magnitude; its back lobe vanishes identically in the far field. The unidirectional behavior is quantified at any finite far-field radius by a closed-form front-to-back ratio, obtained from an exact per-degree cancellation of the electric and magnetic multipole contributions in the backward direction. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) of these elements inherit the SDEU behavior. Driving the arrays with zero-area pulses (ZAPs) transfers the frequency-domain performance intact into the time domain. It is shown that whether the radiated energy beam is narrower or wider than the corresponding intensity beam is decided by a single property of the radiated waveform, not by the size of the radiating aperture. A simple single-cycle ZAP is used to quantify the performance of the UCAs; its energy beam is the narrower one. The same criterion is shown to govern the focal spot of near-field-focused pulse-driven arrays. A custom-designed intensity-enhancement (IE) ZAP is introduced that raises the focal intensity by almost 200-fold over a narrow-band reference while producing a focal spot more than ten times smaller in both the axial and transverse directions, deeply subwavelength with respect to its own effective wavelength. It is demonstrated that these stunning IE results are produced simply with an array of pulse-excited Huygens dipole sources. These results identify the pulse shape, rather than the aperture, as the design variable that governs localized electromagnetic energy and information delivery.

AI.tldr: A vector spherical wave expansion designs an elemental multipole source that radiates a superdirective, extremely unidirectional needle beam; uniform circular arrays of these elements inherit the behavior, and zero-area pulse excitation transfers the frequency-domain performance to the time domain. Pulse shape, not aperture size, is identified as the variable controlling localized electromagnetic energy and information delivery, enabling deeply subwavelength focal spots and strong intensity enhancement.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to enable effective power and information transfer through highly directional radiated beams and to determine whether localized electromagnetic delivery is governed by the radiating aperture or by the radiated waveform.
AI.method: The authors use a vector spherical wave expansion to engineer an elemental multipole source with a superdirective, extremely unidirectional needle beam. They prove analytically and confirm numerically that the element reaches Harrington's normal-directivity value on its beam axis, derive a closed-form front-to-back ratio from exact cancellation of electric and magnetic multipole contributions in the backward direction, and extend the design to uniform circular arrays. The arrays are driven with zero-area pulses, including a simple single-cycle pulse and a custom intensity-enhancement pulse; near-field-focused pulse-driven arrays and arrays of pulse-excited Huygens dipole sources are also analyzed.
AI.result: The elemental source attains Harrington's normal-directivity value along its axis, radiates a linearly polarized field with azimuthally symmetric magnitude, and has an identically vanishing far-field back lobe. Uniform circular arrays inherit the superdirective, extremely unidirectional behavior, and zero-area pulse driving preserves the frequency-domain performance in the time domain. Whether the energy beam is narrower or wider than the intensity beam is shown to depend on a single waveform property rather than aperture size; for a single-cycle zero-area pulse, the energy beam is narrower. The same criterion governs the focal spot of near-field-focused pulse-driven arrays. A custom intensity-enhancement zero-area pulse raises focal intensity by almost 200-fold over a narrow-band reference and produces a focal spot more than ten times smaller in both axial and transverse directions, deeply subwavelength relative to its effective wavelength, using an array of pulse-excited Huygens dipole sources.
AI.conclusion: The pulse shape, rather than the aperture, is the design variable governing localized electromagnetic energy and information delivery. Superdirective multipole elements and their uniform circular arrays, combined with zero-area pulse excitation, provide a route to highly unidirectional beams and deeply subwavelength, intensity-enhanced focusing.

title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method
summary: Fluid flow networks, from pipeline infrastructure to biological vasculature, are governed by nonlinear edgewise hyperbolic laws coupled through continuity and conservation at junctions. Many-query tasks require rapid evaluation across unseen parametric settings, but conventional methods re-solve the system for each query at prohibitive cost. Existing physics-informed neural approaches impose the governing equations through penalty losses over generic neural approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, with no guarantee that their reduction reduces solution error, and the resulting optimization is prone to ill-conditioning, particularly for hyperbolic systems. Building on the "representation-then-projection" principle of the neural basis method, we introduce a new approach for modeling fluid flow networks. Fixed neural bases define the representation space on each edge, while projection of the discretized equations determines the expansion coefficients, embedding edgewise laws into a conservative formulation. Edge subdomains are coupled through non-overlapping domain decomposition, and a neural operator learns, directly in this reduced space, the parametric map to the expansion coefficients. On looped and branching network topologies, we reproduce references with relative $L^2$ errors below 0.02%, whereas the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. Across unseen boundary conditions in both interpolation and extrapolation, we maintain mean pressure errors below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%, while the physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors. These results highlight the framework's potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a neural basis method combining fixed neural bases, projection of discretized fluid-network equations, and a neural operator to rapidly predict nonlinear transient dynamics across unseen parameters and boundary conditions.
AI.motivation: Many-query fluid-flow-network tasks require fast evaluation under unseen parametric settings, but conventional re-solving is prohibitively costly. Existing physics-informed neural approaches use penalty losses over generic approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, do not guarantee reduced solution error, and can be ill-conditioned, especially for hyperbolic systems.
AI.method: Building on representation-then-projection, fixed neural bases define per-edge representation spaces; projection of discretized equations determines expansion coefficients and embeds edgewise laws in a conservative formulation. Non-overlapping domain decomposition couples edge subdomains, and a neural operator learns the parametric map directly in the reduced space to the expansion coefficients.
AI.result: On looped and branching topologies, relative L2 errors are below 0.02%, while the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. For unseen boundary conditions in interpolation and extrapolation, mean pressure errors remain below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%; a physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors.
AI.conclusion: The framework shows potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

title: AI-assisted search for self-compressing gigawatt subcycle field waveforms
summary: We explore the physics behind pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and search for the optimal regimes of such compression over the parameter space as laid out by multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers. With the pertinent physical criteria for pulse contrast and no pulse breakup formalized as operational stopping rules, a radical speedup of such search is achieved by delegating its tedious preliminary stages to generative pretrained transformer models. The precise adjustment of self-compression dynamics vis-a-vis the desired compressed pulse output is, however, not yet delegable to AI agents, as the criteria for such search are still largely subjective, operating with fine aspects of subcycle field structure, not yet formalizable as clear search-stopping instructions. An ultimate precision in such subcycle field engineering is attainable via a management of field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes, enabling pulse self-compression to high-power subcycle field waveforms and opening paths toward fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.

AI.tldr: The paper combines multimode nonlinear dynamics in gas-filled hollow fibers with GPT-assisted search to find regimes for high-power subcycle pulse self-compression, reporting major search speedups but not yet AI-delegable precision tuning.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand and optimize pulse self-compression into high-power subcycle field waveforms and to accelerate the search over the parameter space defined by multimode nonlinear dynamics of ultrashort laser pulses in gas-filled hollow fibers.
AI.method: Physical criteria for pulse contrast and no pulse breakup are formalized as operational stopping rules, and the tedious preliminary stages of the parameter-space search are delegated to generative pretrained transformer models. The abstract also identifies management of field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes as a route to precise subcycle field engineering.
AI.result: Delegating preliminary search stages to generative pretrained transformer models produces a radical speedup. However, precise adjustment of self-compression dynamics relative to the desired compressed pulse output is not yet delegable to AI agents because the relevant criteria remain largely subjective and involve fine aspects of subcycle field structure that are not yet formalizable as clear search-stopping instructions. No quantitative speedup or compressed-pulse metrics are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: AI can substantially accelerate the search for self-compression regimes, but precision subcycle field engineering still requires expert judgment and better-formalized criteria. Managing field-phase-sensitive nonlinear processes is identified as a path to high-power subcycle pulse self-compression and fiber-optic attosecond lightwave engineering.

title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

AI.tldr: Mid-infrared pumping of phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption in NiO, probed by time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at finite momentum, reveals a light-induced two-magnon signal that grows on a 4 ps timescale and decays in 28±11 ps, more than two orders of magnitude longer than previously reported two-magnon dephasing, while the one-magnon energy and linewidth remain essentially unchanged.
AI.motivation: The lifetime, interactions, and decay of correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons, are poorly understood; prior two-magnon measurements showed broad linewidths or coherences dephasing within 200 fs, unlike the well-studied damping of single magnons.
AI.method: The authors pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses far below its bandgap and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum using time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), examining one-magnon energy and linewidth and a pump-induced two-magnon signal on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side.
AI.result: The one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating preserved long-range magnetic order without photocarrier-induced demagnetization. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the anti-Stokes side, peaks 4 ps after the pump despite 0.5 ps time resolution, suggesting delayed growth likely from momentum redistribution across the Brillouin zone, and decays with a 28±11 ps time constant, exceeding prior two-magnon dephasing by more than two orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, analogous to higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.

AI.tldr: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network in western Slovakia uses a central entangled-photon source and passive wavelength routing to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed three-city sub-network, with the fourth city connected via the central node. All reported key rates come after full post-processing and real-time ETSI GS QKD 014 key delivery. The network achieves 13.5 bit/s over 109 km and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB accumulated loss between cities without a direct fiber link; finite-key benchmarking shows heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound and that error correction could raise finite-key rates by a factor of 4.1–6.6 and enable a positive rate on a 142.9 km link.

The work aims to demonstrate a deployed entanglement-based QKD segment within a national quantum communication infrastructure, with real-time key delivery and benchmarking against finite-key security bounds rather than raw coincidence estimates.
AI.method: Polarization-entangled photons are generated at a central node and passively routed by wavelength over deployed telecommunication fiber connecting four cities in western Slovakia. The architecture forms a trusted-node-free, fully meshed three-city sub-network, with the fourth city connected through the central node, and all links operate simultaneously. A matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing supports algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Key rates are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014, using partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation and benchmarking against finite-key security bounds.
